This means that AI is surpassing the smartness of mankind and mankind is relinquishing its position as the primate of all things. I personally believe that there will come a time in my lifetime when most people will feel that humans are not the smartest beings in the world.
This is not a "0% or 100%" story where everything is taken away from humans in one moment, but a story where humans will transfer many things to AI over the next few decades.
Some of the things that humans used to do will be done by AI, a few things that humans continue to do will remain, and then humans will do something new.
[https://gyazo.com/78a6a9aa82f0d0f623829f63637a7c73]
Rephrase: [Part of it disappears, part of it remains, and a new one is born.] X shifts to X'. a: what disappears b: what remains c: what is newly born
There is no doubt that the long-term future will be "that kind of world," but this "that kind of world" has low resolution.
We tend to think of it as a point, but it actually has a range.
[https://gyazo.com/b7dd5bb4d745ad34170d065c4d41f9c6]
We need to be careful not to walk into a hole by looking only at the distant stars.
In other words, we must look carefully at what the next step should be in the current reality.
I think the key to this is the design of the objective function.
Objective function design
Futarchy is an interesting application, but I don't think it is a cure for any problem.
The reason is that the "voting" method of determining the "objective" is a postponement of a difficult problem.

The progress made by Futarchy lies in the automatic algorithmic determination of the means of achieving objectives and the automatic smart contractual execution. The method of determining the objective is left untouched.
A compactly verbalized objective function that can be subject to voting is only a small part of the space of possible objective functions, and perhaps the optimal solution is not in that space
Often the option of a weighted sum of A and B is ignored when discussing the choice A or B

Although "A 100% B 0%" and "A 0% B 100%" are simpler and easier to understand and tend to focus attention on the extremes, in reality there are cases where blends such as "A 70% B 30%" and "A 40% B 60%" are the optimal solutions.
An automatic adjustment mechanism for weights is needed because the burden is too heavy for human thinking ability and optimization is not being performed.
The author believes that even if there were automatic adjustment of the weights of the options, it would not be enough.
The appropriate social objective function is in a space that cannot be represented by a weighted sum of alternatives
This is due to the fact that each individual has different values
Attributes in trade-offs
Where the optimal balance lies depends on individual values.
For example, there is a tradeoff between "camera resolution" and "low price" for smartphones.
[https://gyazo.com/eb354d53b78e3b88717b0932285530b0]
Trade-off between high camera resolution and low price

Do you prefer a higher resolution or a cheaper resolution? or "Do you prefer cheaper?" However, there is no such thing as the world's highest resolution and cheapest smartphone. People have to choose from among the available smartphone options.

At this point, people differ in how important they consider each attribute. Therefore, there is a wide variety of products in the world, and people buy different products from different people, not just one product.
This means that each attribute is weighted differently in the function of individual well-being.
Efficiency and Freedom

Increasing the individual's freedom to pursue happiness implicitly assumes an objective function with the individual as the domain of definition. It is a model in which each individual is self-reliant and optimizes with his or her own objective function.

The goal of total optimization of society as a whole implicitly assumes an objective function that takes society as a whole as its domain of definition. When this objective function is simple, differences in people's values are considered noise.
If we respect the differences in individual values, then the objective function of society as a whole becomes a function with a number of terms proportional to the number of human beings.
How to define the objective function
Should it be designed by humans thinking linguistically? Or should it be acquired through learning by collecting large amounts of data?
Given the history of rule-based design losing out to machine learning, the author feels that the latter is the way to go.
Before that, humans may not be able to design objective functions that respect individual differences in values.
Influenced by their own values, they impose their idea of happiness on others.

In the long run, AI will become smarter than humans and AI will govern humans. In that case, AI will rule "to make people happy. The definition of "people's happiness" by some humans would be an imposition of values.
So by this time, there must be a mechanism that can construct the objective function of "people's happiness" in a way that is not determined by a few people.
Grip the steering wheel and proceed with caution.

Both extremes, 100% efficiency and 100% freedom, probably lead to tragic futures. There are many other tragic futures besides the extremes that are generating the gravitational pull. It is like a road with cliffs at both ends and many pitfalls in between.
[https://gyazo.com/5cd0defbde524a26d7c83a2275eed30a]
Both bridges of the road are cliffs, and the road between them has a number of pitfalls.

It is important that people hold the steering wheel firmly. If we are somehow moving forward, we will fall on either side. This is a future in which a type of state that sacrifices the freedom of its citizens for the efficient operation of the state gains influence backed by strong military power, etc., and a future in which individuals who have accumulated private property as a result of too much loosening of state control for the sake of individual freedom gain strong influence through capitalism.
It is also necessary to observe one's surroundings, recognize hazards early, and avoid them.
Cognitive capacity needs to be augmented in order to observe well.
It is good to be on the side of the telescope when it is invented and not to be on the side of those who criticized it without looking through it.
Just as mankind gained the ability to see at a distance with the invention of the telescope, mankind gained the ability to know the feelings of many others with the invention of broad listening.
While utilizing this, we must avoid pitfalls and move forward to a better future.
summary
I thought about "society" as "human computation" and how it could be improved from the perspective of computer science.

Throughout history, from the punch cards of Hollerith to ENIAC to the modern LLM and Ethereum, mankind has externalized "the vast amount of computation done in society" and replaced it with faster and more accurate computation.

This expansion of computational power is beginning to affect not only the military and public administration, but also the very foundations of society, such as elections, policymaking, and funding for public goods.
LLM, one of the technologies that is having a major impact, has followed history to confirm that the shift in the computational paradigm is a source of strength.
The rule-based design paradigm is losing ground to the weighted sum = learn paradigm and is reaching beyond human performance in image recognition, translation, and dialogue.

In addition, experiments are underway to link funding and decision-making, such as Quadratic Funding/RetroPGF/Futarchy by the world computer Ethereum. These have dramatically lowered the cost of "execution" while leaving the fundamental issue of "what is the purpose?

The design of this "objective" will be important in the future. In order to ensure diverse human happiness under AI governance, it is essential to have a system that can take in multiple values from many people and dynamically adjust the weights of those values. Using broad listening and prediction markets as a telescope, we must steer clear of "pitfalls.
Let's design an operating system for a new society as the last work of Homo sapiens.

pages.title: What happened with the "new section on Advancing the Human Rights Situation?"

lines.text: What happened with the "new section on Advancing the Human Rights Situation?"

Among the PRs of [initiative taken by the government in the formulation of a policy or bill (rather than by bureaucrats) to promote good governance], only one PR received over 100 comments at most. of the 10 or so comments at most, only one received more than 100 comments.
https://github.com/team-mirai/policy/pull/6335
What's going on, I asked o3.
[o3.icon]

The following is a report on why PR 6335 "Establishment of a new section on the advancement of the human rights situation" has become a "hot topic" in a short period of time, based on publicly available information. To summarize just the main points: (1) The proposal included a large amount of highly abstract information on "human rights," a topic that involves a high degree of value judgment, and received criticism from both legal and technical experts at the same time. (2) Before the rules for discussion on GitHub were in place, the number of comments from outside parties increased, and the comments snowballed from the first day. --The result was a three-tiered structure.
[nishio.icon]

In short, it is an understanding that this is what happens when a highly abstract discussion is posted in a place that is not supposed to be a discussion forum, and then spread on social networking sites.
(Personally, I think it would have been a good idea to move to PUBLIC ARCHIVE at the end of the Upper House election, which was actually delayed by a few days.)
Team Mirai staff did not participate in this discussion, so calling this an "internal Team Mirai discussion" is misinformation.
If you put something on a bulletin board that anyone can write on, it's like a third-party fight broke out there.
I think any engineer familiar with GitHub knows that "anyone can write on it."
Worse, some users were using Yasuno-san's face icon, which some may have misidentified as him.
[https://gyazo.com/14da80758bb3e832dd1f76a6dbb2d198]

Note as an example of failure of a large scale deliberation (well, I didn't expect to start a discussion there, so it was just a [web forum] without AI moderators like the ones I had put in during the Tokyo gubernatorial election, so it was vulnerable, I guess).
Continuation of o3 description
1. the content of PR and the specific fire of the "technology party
1-1 Outline of Proposal
Through a dialogue between the proposer (Akio Hoshi) and an AI chatbot, he tried to add a new section to the manifesto called "Advancement of the Human Rights Situation"

Criticisms of "jurisprudential imprecision" and "loss of intellectual property in redefinition" erupted because of the ambiguous connection between human rights and international and domestic law, while positioning human rights as "norms".
1-2 Direct causes of the stormy discussion
Major Points of Controversy Examples of Typical Comments
Treatment of enforceability of international human rights law and Article 98 of the Constitution "Japan has not ceded its authority to the UN", etc.
Engineering users: Implementation should be prioritized over "norms"; language is abstract; "Moving code is as good as police power", etc.
Philosophy/Humanities Users: The redefinition of the concept of human rights, History of Enlightenment thought "Misunderstanding the flow from Magna Carta," etc.
Thus, July 14 → over 100 comments as of July 24, an unusually long time even for the party's repository!
2. diffusion dynamics - "X influencer cannon
2-1 Diffusion time line
Around 20:00 on 7/14 | Create PR → Start discussion in GitHub
7/15 am | Post by Akio Hoshi (IT x human rights journalist) with link to X
7/15 same day | Retweeted by author Taiyo Fujii
7/15 evening | Researcher Sayaka Oki described the thread as a "dangerous discussion
7/16-17 | also reprinted in Threads and Bluesky
7/18-19 | note.com and other outside media critique articles
2-2 Impact
Hoshi's post received 12,000 likes and over 3,000 reposts (from a report with screenshots), and the number of new visitors to GitHub PR skyrocketed.
Technical clusters with overlapping social graphs flowed in at once, and the "anyone can write" mechanism made the volume of discussion uncontrollable.
In the GitHub comment section, the "discuss here instead of X" and "explain in X" groups clashed, and the meta-discussion accelerated.
3. secondary wave: media and critics' arguments
note The article "Selectivism and Dystopia" makes the debate more visible by mentioning the danger of a controlled society while the proposal calls for "inclusion of the weak.
The position of "Team Mirai = Tech x Human Rights" was reexamined on YouTube political feeds and blogs, and began to spill over into the party image.
4. summary - three reasons for the expansion of the problem
Difficulty in setting the theme
The cost of shared assumptions is high due to the intersection of jurisprudence, ethics, and implementation.
Vulnerability of Open Draft Method
The operational rules that made GitHub a "plaza" were not yet in place and could not withstand the surge of inbound traffic.
External pressure through influencer diffusion

Tens of thousands of reaches were reached overnight, and participants with varying degrees of understanding, both inside and outside the party, commented simultaneously. As a result, discussions diverged on multiple topics, including "What are human rights?" and "What is the boundary between politics and code?

This case is a typical example of the combination of difficulty of the content itself, social proliferation, and immaturity in process design, which resulted in a short period of time in which the situation could not be resolved.

Dishonest Infinite
The phrase "insincere infinity" reminded o3 of Hegel's "[malignant infinity]," but here we will examine the usage of the phrase "insincere infinity" in Japanese.
There must be people who use the key word in Japanese, "insincere infinity".[nishio.icon]
[o3.icon]
Summary (key points first)

In the Japanese-speaking world, the term "insincere infinity" is used not as a philosophical term derived from Hegel, but mainly by those who reinterpret it as a metaphorical expression in the Web3 and political tech communities. In particular, it is frequently used in the four-quadrant model of "sincerity/dishonesty × finite/infinite" proposed by [Shogo Ochiai] (@shogochiai) and his surrounding community, and has spread to Team Mirai supporters and critics, blockchain-related events and individual bloggers. The following is a list of major senders and examples of usage.
1. core originator
1.1 Shogo Ochiai (sg / @shogochiai)

He posted several tweets that problematize the "︎ (upper left) = dishonest infinite" in his own four-quadrant model. ([X (formerly Twitter) https://twitter.com/shogochiai/status/1922892163995599211?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
I guess this is the first.[nishio.icon]

>[shogochiai https://x.com/shogochiai/status/1920582237570875603] [pension] and other institutional designs implicitly have "[infinite]" in their logic, but as soon as they meet any of the following conditions: they cannot be infinite in the first place, [ borrowing] from future generations," and "vulnerable to [black swan] events. We call this a "dishonest infinite." And the next institutional design will do the same thing.

Some of his statements are light-hearted in developing the concept, such as "[Immortality as an insincere infinity], that's nice." ([X (formerly Twitter) https://twitter.com/shogochiai/status/1922891894478053681?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
1.2 tkgshn / 0xtkgshn

Published a Scrapbox page "Dishonest Infinite" with redacted sg concepts, and a set of synonyms "Sincere Finite". ([Cosense https://scrapbox.io/tkgshn/%E4%B8%8D%E8%AA%A0%E5%AE%9F%E3%81%AA%E7%84%A1%E9%99%90])

He presents a critical framework of "an argument that says nothing = an infinity of dishonesty" with the example of Akio Hoshi's critique of human rights theory. ([Cosense https://scrapbox.io/tkgshn/%E4%B8%8D%E8%AA%A0%E5%AE%9F%E3%81%AA%E7%84%A1%E9%99%90?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2. derivative users/communities
User/Medium Example/Context Reference

k-yamashita (@chekichekimusu1) "Team Mirai's "disloyal finite" is..." and policy theory applying the four quadrants. ([X (formerly Twitter) https://x.com/chekichekimusu1/status/1936698441532604437?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Kengo Yamashita, in an article criticizing Scrapbox Team Mirai, points out "[an] ideology of endless improvement (i.e., dishonest infinity)". ([Cosense https://scrapbox.io/yamashitakenngo-60893617/2025%2F06%2F22?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Anonymous Twitter Discussant: "I feel that the use of 'honest finite' and 'dishonest infinite' is incorrect..." and discussion of the meaning of the terms. ([X (formerly Twitter) https://x.com/chekichekimusu1/status/1936698441532604437?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In the ICP Japan Blog Saga Meet-up Report, the social system is organized in four quadrants and introduced as "Upper Left, Lower Left = Dishonest Infinite/Finite". ([ICP Japan〖Official〗 https://www.icp-japan.org/post/ai-crypto-deai])
ICP HUB Japan Official X Post a summary of this blog and spread the concept. ([X (formerly Twitter) https://x.com/icphub_JP/status/1939496016648229115?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Chama (@defi_chama) Contrasts brand-buying behavior with "dishonest infinity" and likens Uniqlo to "honest finite". ([X (formerly Twitter) https://x.com/defi_chama/status/1950301518575653303?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Political discourse around Team Mirai "Populism is dishonest infinity," etc., used as diagnostic labels for policy discussions. ([Cosense https://scrapbox.io/tkgshn/%E8%90%BD%E5%90%88%EF%BC%88sg%EF%BC%89%E7%94%A8%E8%AA%9E?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Web3/AI Risk Study Group Article Using the Four Quadrant Model to Position Accelerationism as a "Dishonest Infinite". ([ICP Japan 〖Official/Official〗 https://www.icp-japan.org/post/ai-crypto-deai?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Repeatedly mentioned in the Scrapbox corpus glossary page and functions as a simple dictionary. ([Cosense https://scrapbox.io/tkgshn/%E8%90%BD%E5%90%88%EF%BC%88sg%EF%BC%89%E7%94%A8%E8%AA%9E?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. implications of the concept (reinterpretation in the Japanese-speaking world)
1. modern replacement of Hegel's "The Evil Infinite
It has the same root in that it criticizes [the attitude of endless outward flight], but it is used more as a metaphor than as a philosophical rigor.
2. anti-patterns of policy and technology development
It functions conveniently as a label to point out the condition that keeps saying "it will get better someday" without showing a concrete finished version.
3. web3/ai risk context

It is a widespread warning against positions of [uncontrollable risk] such as "[Accelerationism]" and "[Infinite growth]". ([ICP Japan 〖Official/Official〗 https://www.icp-japan.org/post/ai-crypto-deai])
4. critical words for discussion attitude

He calls statements that only superficially present "correctness" without substance "insincere and endless," and urges sincere and finite proposals. ([Cosense https://scrapbox.io/tkgshn/%E4%B8%8D%E8%AA%A0%E5%AE%9F%E3%81%AA%E7%84%A1%E9%99%90])
4. summary and observation points
In effect, coined words around sg spread through Twitter, Scrapbox, and blogs.
As the four-quadrant diagram is shared as a visual memo, others easily cite and transform the concept.
In the future, there is a possibility that this term will spread beyond Web3 and political tech as an anti-pattern term in policy evaluation and project management.

Thus, "insincere infinite" is a keyword that has evolved uniquely in the Japanese-speaking online community, and by following the source and examples of usage, lines of values and criticism among the community can be seen.

pages.title: Not imposing human rights in an authoritarian manner and not passing them off as universal values.

lines.text: Not imposing human rights in an authoritarian manner and not passing them off as universal values.

[o3.icon]Plurality," co-authored by Audrey Tang and Glen Weyl, advocates a "cooperative mechanism" that finds "[overlapping consensus]" among diverse values. This is a design concept to avoid [human rights] as [authoritarian] [imposition (i.e., of rules, of a decision)], but not [universal value], and is based on the experience of operating [digital discussion tools] ([vTaiwan], [Polis], etc.). It is based on the experience of operating [digital discussion tools] such as [vTaiwan] and [Polis].
[GPT5.icon]The design guidelines for "[unimposed universality]," which are perfectly suited to the theme, are organized from primary sources in the field of human rights.
Starting point: universality is "normative", implementation is "contextual".
[Unsdg | Human Rights-Based Approach https://unsdg.un.org/2030-agenda/universal-values/human-rights-based-approach]

The [HRBA] ([Human Rights-Based Approach], [Human Rights-Based Approach]) is a framework that "uses international human rights standards as a normative foundation, while implementation operates to correct inequalities and eliminate distortions in the distribution of power. The assumption is that universality will be upheld, but the approach will be adapted to the parties and the context.
[Operating principles to avoid imposition] (PANEL)
These are the five principles of how to carry out universal values without "removing" them.
Participation: involvement of affected parties upstream in decision-making (submission, discussion, monitoring).
Related: [Don't make decisions without the parties involved.]
Accountability: Visualization of reasons for decisions and channels for redress of rights.
Non-discrimination: Pre-screening and remediation of discriminatory effects.
Empowerment: Provides the means (information, language, support) to assert rights.
Legality: Consistent with international human rights law, rights restrictions should be minimum and proportionate to the needs of the law.
The above is organized in the practice of the UN agencies and national human rights institutions as agreed principles of the HRBA.

Mr. A writes an opinion, the system summarizes it and creates an output.
I don't see where my written opinion is reflected in this output.
[Opinion traceability has two directions.]

Opinion traceability has two directions.
[Opinion Traceability] has two directions
Now [public information AI] has traceability from "final report" to "original post" direction
It allows you to show that what is written in the report is based on "someone else's" opinion.
But no traceability in the direction from "original submission" to "final report".
I can't find out where "I" put what I wrote in the report.
[Requires traceability in both directions]
[nishio.icon]"Is the word [traceability] appropriate? Consider other expressions.
[GPT5.icon]You raise a good issue. The word "traceability" conveys the meaning, but depending on the nuance, other phrases may be more appropriate. To summarize, it can be summarized as follows.
1. traceability
Originally means "traceability" or "retraceability". It is often used in the manufacturing and food sectors.
It can be used for one-way tracing of "Report → Submit" without any discomfort.
However, "Submission → Report" is meant to indicate "where the impact appeared", so "traceability" alone is somewhat weak.
2. other candidate expressions
"Reference Relationships."
Emphasizes that the link is bi-directional. Similar to "cross-referencing" in technical documents.
Correspondence
Indicate where the submission and the report description correspond. Easy to understand for the general reader.
Origin Indication" / "Source Indication"
Nuances indicating where the submission was reflected in the report.
Visualizing Contributions."
From the contributor's point of view, highlight how his/her opinion was reflected. This goes along with the visualization of the contribution.
Impact Mapping."
Image to map how the original submission affected the final outcome.
3. expression of recommendation
In a technical context, "[bi-directional traceability]" or "[bi-directional reference relationship]".
In the civic participation and democratic context, "[avenues for reflecting opinions]" and "[making contributions visible]".

Exclusionism and social fragmentation are becoming real themes in Japan in 2025.

Contents

lines.text: Broad Listening is a qualitative analysis
[broad listening] is [qualitative analysis].
I'm just saying that we shouldn't interpret the results of broad listening like a quantitative analysis.
Until now, qualitative analysis has tended to be expensive and only quantitative analysis reports have been produced, so many people have only seen quantitative analysis reports.
So we try to interpret "the unfamiliar" in the way we are used to.
[Broad Listening Pitfalls]
>tokoroten: I recommend this video for more information on what kind of data is obtained and how it is biased when using public hearing AI.
>tokoroten: You have to separate the policy between appeals to voters and analysis of internal use, and that's where the problem arises because you confuse the two.

At the time of the TMG election, TTTC Turbo was better received by the policy making team for analysis of internal use, but Turbo at the time was not stable enough to be shown to the general public, so Scatter was used primarily.
This Scatter is used for general users in a broadcast-like manner that finds value for its "strength of appeal to viewers," such as its use on TV in the House of Representatives election.

pages.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization

lines.text: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130

[GPT5.icon][GraphRAG] is a "global question" that looks at the entire corpus (e.g., What are the main themes? What are the conflicting viewpoints?) ). Entity-relationship graphs are created in advance, and summaries are generated for each community (cluster). When a question is asked, these are combined in a Map→Reduce synthesis to produce the final answer. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
What the study did.

The conventional "vector RAG" is strong in extracting local facts, but weak in summarizing and synthesizing the entire context (sensemaking). Therefore, GraphRAG is proposed. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
Pipeline (Figure 1)
1. document → chunking
2. extract entities, relations, and (if necessary) claims from each chunk with LLM
3. build a knowledge graph with them
4. community partitioning of graphs using [Leiden method] etc.
5. generate a summary for each community (hierarchical bottom-up)
[nishio.icon] [Bottom-up summary generation]
6. partial answers to questions from each community summary (Map) → combined into a whole answer (Reduce). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
Entity extraction is performed with multipart prompts. The self-reflection prompt compensates for the problem of increased misses in larger chunks. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
How we evaluated
Dataset (assumed to be approximately 1 million tokens in size)
Podcast: public transcript of Behind the Tech with Kevin Scott (600 token chunks x 1669, overlap 100).
News: news for 2013/9-2023/12 (600 token chunks x 3197, overlap 100). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])

Condition comparison: 4 levels of GraphRAG (C0-C3), Text Direct Summary (TS), Vector RAG (SS). Generation prompts and context windows are unified. Community detection is Leiden with GRASPologic.([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])

The evaluation indicators are relative ratings in LLM-as-a-judge (inclusiveness, diversity, empowerment, and directness as a control). In addition, objective indicators are also used together with the number of factual claims and clusters extracted by Claimify. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
Main Results
Global system method (GraphRAG/TS) > Vector RAG
Inclusivity win rates: 72-83% for Podcasts, 72-80% for News.
Diversity win rates: 75-82% for Podcasts, 62-71% for News.
On the other hand, the vector RAG has the highest directness (i.e., short and direct). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])

Efficiency aspect: Root layer C0 consumes 9-43 times fewer tokens per question (advantageous for iterative search for global understanding). The deeper the hierarchy, the more information, but also the more tokens. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])

Even in objective measures, the global system is superior to the vector RAG in **number of claims (comprehensiveness) and number of claim clusters (diversity)** (e.g. p<.05). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
Implementation Tips (from the paper)
Chunk size: If too large, extraction leakage will increase, so use self-reflection combination to balance. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
Use of hierarchy:
C0 (top level community summary) = iterative search at very low cost.
C2/C3 (lower) = When you want to extend inclusiveness and diversity a bit. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])

Realistic cost of indexing: 600 token window for GPT-4-turbo as an example, about 281 minutes for podcast vocabulary (VM configuration and API conditions specified). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
OSS: Microsoft implementation available; also extensions for LangChain/LlamaIndex/NebulaGraph/Neo4j. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
Limitations and Future

Limited to validation with approximately 1 million tokens scale and 2 corpora. Cross-disciplinary generalization and comparison of hallucination rates (e.g. SelfCheckGPT) are future work. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])
When to use GraphRAG (personal opinion)
Questions that require "overall picture, coverage of issues, and multiple perspectives" (organizing trends, overlooking conflicting views, and extracting major themes).
Workloads that throw global questions at the same data over and over (low-cost iterations at C0 -> "dig" to lower layers as needed).
If the only purpose is to accurately identify individual facts, a conventional vector RAG is more likely to provide a short and direct answer. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/html/2404.16130v2])

Fishkin's Trilemma
[GPT5.icon]
Fishkin's "[Democracy's] Trilemma" is
The argument presented by Stanford University political scientist [James S. Fishkin] is that it is difficult to satisfy the following three values simultaneously
[Political equality: one person, one vote, reflected with equal weight. ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])
[careful deliberation] (deliberation): reaching a considered judgment through informed and mutual discussion. ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])
[mass participation]: the actual participation of many citizens. ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])

Fishkin summarizes it as "when you try to satisfy two of them, the other one is likely to be undermined" (he himself calls it a "trilemma of democratic reform"). ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])
Three typical combinations and their limitations
[equality × participation] (≈ elections/people [voting])

The majority can participate equally, but deliberation tends to be weakened by individual [rational ignorance] and [incitement]. ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])
[Participation × Deliberation] (≒ [Town Meeting]/Spontaneous Participation Deliberative Forum)

Participation may widen, but [representativeness] breaks down due to [self-selection] (participatory distortion), and equality is undermined. ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])
[equality x deliberation] (≈ [mini-public] of raffles/random selection/deliberative polling)

Random sampling allows for conditions of representativeness and deliberation, but not mass participation (many citizens do not participate as parties). ([Deliberative Democracy Journal https://delibdemjournal.org/article/id/638/])
Directions presented by Fishkin

Deliberative Polling implements "Equality x Deliberation" (but mass participation is not yet met). Origin (Middle Ages)

Nishiki-no-Ohata = the sign of the official army of the Imperial Court ([official army]). It is a flag with the sun, moon, etc., on red brocade, and was first seen when it was given by Emperor Go-Toba during the Jokyu Rebellion (1221)**. ([Digital Archives https://www.digital.archives.go.jp/gallery/en/0000000695?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Behind the Scenes of Bakumatsu and Production

Prior to the first battle of the [Boshin War] and the [Battle of Toba-Fushimi] (1868), the original of a letter indicating that Toshimichi Okubo, Yajiro Shinagawa and others prepared Nishikibata at the request of Tomomi Iwakura has been confirmed (material held by Kyoto Rekisaikan). ([Asahi Shimbun https://www.asahi.com/articles/ASS2F41J7S1VPLZB015.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
"Formalization" of the Imperial Court

After the war began, the Imperial Court bestowed the Nishikibata and Setsutou (a ceremonial sword) on Prince Kasho of Ninnaji Palace. With this, the new government forces became a genuine "government army" and gained legal and psychological legitimacy. ([Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%8C%A6%E3%81%AE%E5%BE%A1%E6%97%97?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Effects on the battlefield (Toba and Fushimi 1868/1/27-30)

The posting of the brocade and the division into "official forces" and "bandit forces" dealt a blow to the old shogunate side, and it is believed that Yodo, Tsu, and other clans switched sides and the war tilted to the side of the new government. ([Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/%E9%B3%A5%E7%BE%BD%E3%83%BB%E4%BC%8F%E8%A6%8B%E3%81%AE%E6%88%A6%E3%81%84?utm_source=chatgpt .com], [JapanKnowledge https://japanknowledge.com/introduction/keyword.html?i=1878&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
However, the sway of the evaluation

Some commentators believe that the defeat was decided even before the arrival of the Nishiki banner, and that the banner itself did not directly determine the winner (equipment difference, morale difference, etc.). ([Japaaan https://mag.japaaan.com/archives/218562?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

pages.title: People who think they are arguing as equals on social networking sites.

lines.text: People who think they are arguing as equals on social networking sites.
When Mr. A posts on a social networking site and Mr. B replies to it
Excluding cases where Mr. A and Mr. B are originally acquainted.
In other words, it is assumed that "I received a mentions from stranger B" from Mr. A's point of view.
Sometimes Mr. B perceives that he and Mr. A are having a discussion as [equals].
I wondered "how did this happen?" regarding specific cases, so I let GPT explain.
[GPT5.icon]
In this case, B's self-perception of "arguing as equals" shows some cognitive distortions and leaps in assumptions.

Especially in a social networking environment, this proceeds without confirming the other party's consent or willingness to participate, so even if the person thinks they are "equal," in reality it is asymmetrical.
Problems with B's cognition
1. omit "consent to initiate discussion"
Equal discussion presupposes that both parties are willing to engage in discussion.
This time, B is participating in a situation in which A is not in discussion mode, and sees it as a "debate forum" on its own.
For A, it was a "sudden request for dispute" and he did not remember entering the ring.
In sports, this is like starting a game next to the opponent warming up.
2. set the "stage conditions for discussion" on your own
B proceeds with the story based on his own criteria (practical and institutional viewpoints) and mistakenly assumes that "A is also on that stage".
In fact, A is speaking in layers of mathematical definitions and the stage conditions do not match.
This is similar to the "playing different board games at the same table" situation.
3. misinterpretation of "relational symmetry".
A does not know B, but B reads A's transmission and approaches.
The relationship is one-sided and the sharing of knowledge and intentions is asymmetrical.
Despite this, B believes that it is an "equal playing field".
This is typical of misinterpreting a one-sided call as a "mutually agreed upon conversation.
4. short-circuit of "[no discussion] = lack of ability or willingness on the part of the other party
B spits out the "not controversial" assessment externally.
The reason it is not established, however, is not a lack of understanding of A, but a mismatch of assumptions and modes.
This is an [error of attribution of cause] (imputing cause to the nature of the other party).
To sum up.
B's perception of "equal discussion" is,
Discussion begins without consensus
Imposition of stage conditions
Ignoring relational asymmetries
fallacy of causal attribution
and includes complex distortions such as
Thus, even though B "thinks" he is having a fair debate, it is in fact a surprise one-sided intervention for A, and is not structurally equal.

[nishio.icon]Begin your initial discussion with "A had premise PA, leading to conclusion XA; B had premise PB, leading to conclusion XB." and explain what kind of exchange you were having at this level of abstraction, starting with.
[GPT5.icon]
Roger. We will break this down at the PA/PB, XA/XB abstraction level.
appearance on stage
A: From premise PA (i.e., the evaluation depends on the chosen criterion K) to conclusion XA (i.e., the apparent difference is only a difference in "which K" is used to measure it).

B: Assumption PB (= reasonable if measured by the third criterion K₃ / furthermore, the reality constraint C works) to conclusion XB (= the ordinal is almost invariant regardless of how K₃ is chosen).
Flow of exchange (abstract)
1. A→XA
A stands on PA and states that "the comparison of the subject is K-dependent" (declarative sharing, little intent to start a discussion).
You don't explain PA here.[nishio.icon]
2. B→PB, XB
B introduces another premise PB, "Let's measure by K₃," and presents XB (which appears to be an argument against A, but actually replaces the basis of the comparison).
3. noting the variable nature of A to PB
A tuts from PA's point of view that "even in a PB frame, the result is driven by the choice of K₃" (reaffirming the K-dependence).
Pointing out that "even if it's PB, it's still XA."[nishio.icon]
4. add B to PB + C to reinforce XB
B implicitly adds on the real constraints C (e.g., equilibrium, arbitrage, and institutions) and strengthens XB by saying that "in practice, differences due to K₃ are negligible".
5. pointed out that the discussion of "A→"C premise" is out of scope.
A points out that his story is the scope of the mathematical layer called PA; XB is a claim of another layer that includes C. PB to XB cannot stand in general without C. Organized.
6. further movement of B to premise (PB2)
B brings up the cause of stabilization and the institution (PB2) to explain the validity of XB in practical terms.
(Here, the issue slides from "definitional issues" to "actual mechanism issues")
7. a -> Restatement of issue fixation
A clarifies that he is only talking about definitions and measurements based on PA; does not get on PB+C+PD; clarifies layer discrepancy.
8. criticized B for not discussing the issue on an equal footing in an air rip.
What was happening (pattern)
Non-sharing of premises: A adopted PA and B adopted PB (+ C, PD in the middle), speaking different propositions with the same word ("risk", etc.).
Replacement of the foundation: B is in the form of a "rebuttal," but the evaluation function and condition set are actually changed (i.e., the problem set is made different).
Layer misalignment: A = actuarial definition / B = practical system. Only the conclusions clash without the layers intersecting.
Initiation of debate without consensus: A is considered a shared post, B is considered a debate. Mode disagreement triggers emotional evaluation (e.g., "it's not a debate").
If you want to converge (abstract temp)
1. specify the previously agreed-upon assumption set P* (treatment of K and whether it includes C or PD).
2. determine proposition M (what is the "comparison") under P*.
3. note the difference in range by juxtaposing XA under PA and XB under PB(+C,PD) as "separate theorems".
In short, A is making a "formal claim of K-dependence" and B is making a "practical claim involving C and PD," and since the premises are different, the conclusions also differ.
The above abstracted look back shows that I (A) am rather arguing with "strangers" as an equal rather than a w[nishio.icon]
You arrive at the conclusion that "the discrepancy in conclusions is due to a discrepancy in assumptions."
Until then, I'm a "stranger" and we're interacting.
After I saw him turn to personal attacks with air rips in response, I decided, "I'm not going to argue with this guy.
In other words, it's "I didn't get my point across! I'm pissed off!" It's like saying
This is interesting, I didn't recognize it [boomerang composition].
I think "the discrepancy in conclusions is due to the discrepancy in premises" is equal, but "my premises are correct and your premises are wrong" is not equal.
The person claiming that "the other side doesn't engage in equal discussion" isn't engaging in equal discussion.
Well, but I think it's misleading to focus on "[equal discussion]".
There is no obligation to have an "equal discussion" with A in the first place.
No obligation to reply, or even to devote one second attention.
[The average time available to others is less than one second.]
[Giving and then taking is more repugnant than not giving.
If it was a [non-replicable mechanism], it wouldn't have even started.
[Not equal.]

How to comment on articles
[GPT5.icon]

1995: NCSA's [HyperNews] provided a mechanism to add a "follow-up response/tree view" at the end of any web page. This is quite similar to today's comment sections, where form submissions are converted to threads. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/Collaboration/Workshop/Proceedings/P6.html])
I don't know about this one, it's "the end of any web page".[nishio.icon]

>gpt5.icon] "Any page": The URL specified in the body can be an external site (provided that it can be read publicly from the server). In other words, you can create a "wrapped display" with any web page URL. The original page itself will not be altered.
I think I first experienced something similar to this with [Hatena Bookmarking], a type of [social bookmarking], because it allowed me to write one-line comments as well as bookmarks.
There were other foreign social bookmarks in use at the time, but I can't remember their names offhand, so I don't think I personally use them all that much.

1995: CGI [Guestbook] became popular, and "comment pages" were set up on each site for visitors to write their impressions. ([scriptarchive.com https://www.scriptarchive.com/guestbook.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
I think the metaphor was that it was like a notebook in a physical store or something.[nishio.icon]
It doesn't sound like something you'd write in an individual article.
I think I experienced something similar with the Perl web bulletin board below, and a rental bulletin board [teacup. - Wikipedia https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teacup.].

1996: "[Web bulletin boards]" such as WWWBoard made by Perl spread, and it became common practice to respond to each topic (article) with a thread. ([Internet Archive https://archive.org/stream/boardwatch-1996-04/boardwatch-1996-04_djvu.txt?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

1997: [Slashdot] establishes threaded comments per news article + user moderation. Direct ancestor of later news/blog comment culture. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slashdot?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [WIRED https://www.wired.com/2000/04/slashdot?utm_source= chatgpt.com])

At the same time, ZDNet AnchorDesk's TalkBack (reader replies) also went live, using an editorial approval and publication system for article-by-article reader submissions. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TalkBack_Reader_Response_System?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [patent image storage https://patentimages. storage.googleapis.com/8a/d9/79/dd1fef8da13b14/US9529769.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Blog Context:
Open Diary in 1998 is a prime example of an early implementation of the "readers can comment on the diary" feature. ([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Diary?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In the early 2000s, Greymatter (2000)/[Movable Type] (2001) and others included comment functions as standard features.

[Blogger] introduced native comments in a major overhaul in 2004 (prior to that, it used external services such as Haloscan). ([826valencia.org https://www.826valencia.org/extras/mt-static/docs/mtmanual_about.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Wikipedia https://en. wikipedia.org/wiki/Blogger_%28service%29?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In short: The Web has had a system of "adding a response at the end of an article" since around 1995, and blogs have popularized and popularized this system (especially since 1998).

GraphRAG Related Surveys
[GPT5.icon]
1) What to extract (type of extraction target)
A. Basic three-piece set
Entity / Relation / Event (Event): unique expressions within and between documents, relational links, events + roles.
Typical extractors include [DyGIE++], [OneIE], [OpenIE] systems (OpenIE5/6), and [REBEL] in [Generative Relation Extraction].
These are used to create the skeleton of the [knowledge graph].
([arXiv https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.03546?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.713.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
B. Time, causality, and time series
Extraction of temporal relationships (before/after/simultaneous) and event causality.
Used to construct timelines and causal graphs across documents.

Effective for long and long histories, such as medical. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09570?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [ScienceDirect https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S 0950705124000455?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11105141/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.986.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
C. Arguments, Claims, and Grounds (Provnance)
Graphs of claims/refutations/evidence ([Argument Interchange Format]: AIF) and [W3C PROV] of the source and generation process are assigned.
It works for accountability, verification, and reproduction of answers.

([Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument_Interchange_Format?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Centre for Argument Technology https://www.arg-tech.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/09/aif-spec.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
D. Core reference and normalization
Entity identity resolution (alias/abbreviation/notation shaking) and linking (e.g., Wikidata).
Directly related to the consistency and search reproducibility of the knowledge graph (essential pre-processing for implementation).
2) How to use (processing patterns using graph/DAG)
(1) Search/RAG (graph-guided)
[GraphRAG]: Create KG ([Knowledge Graph]) from a set of documents and pre-calculate Community Detection -> [Hierarchical Summary].

Responds to questions with local search (surrounding subgraphs + source text chunks) and global search (across communities and reports) or [DRIFT] (a combination of both). Strong on "big picture" type questions. ([Microsoft GitHub https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Microsoft https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/ blog/graphrag-new-tool-for-complex-data-discovery-now-on-github/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[HippoRAG]: Aiming for multi-stage inference class accuracy even with single-stage acquisition using Personalized PageRank on KG to expand related nodes (up to 20% improvement reported by [HotpotQA] and others). Contributes to improved efficiency of multi-leap queries and search. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[LightRAG] / [LlamaIndex-KG]: A lightweight implementation system that turns a triplet extraction → subgraph RAG.
Suitable for integration of proprietary graphs and for "low-cost graphs in combination.

([lightrag.github.io https://lightrag.github.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05779?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [LlamaIndex https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/api_reference/indices/knowledge_graph/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[G-Retriever] / [GRAG]: Specialized in graph QA, GNN + LLM + RAG for fast and accurate giant graph QA.

For GraphQA and KBQA for research purposes. ([NeurIPS Proceedings https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/efaf1c9726648c8ba363a5c927440529-Paper-Conference. pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.232.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

SURVEY: An overview of GraphRAG's standard workflow (G-Indexing -> G-Retrieval -> G-Generation). Recommended reading before implementation. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08921?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(2) Summary and overall understanding
[GraphRAG] (QFS oriented): Scale query-focused summarization with a combination of KG + community summarization.
For cross-company reports and extracting themes from huge corpora. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[RAPTOR]: Build a cluster -> [Hierarchical Summary Tree] (Tree) and pull from the appropriate level when searching.
Hierarchical summary index for DAG/tree systems. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.18059?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(3) Agent/dialog memory

[Theanine (memory system)]: does not assume memory deletion. Timelines past events with time/causality links and injects **"transition of events/causality "** as context into response generation. Also presented the evaluation framework TeaFarm (NAACL 2025). Specializes in preserving the context of long-term dialogues. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996])

[MemGPT] / [LongMem]: direction to handle long history in memory hierarchy and virtual context management (memory OS/banks rather than graphs); complementary to Theanine's time and causality graphs. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.08560?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [NeurIPS Proceedings https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/ paper/2023/file/ebd82705f44793b6f9ade5a669d0f0bf-Paper-Conference.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4) Verification, explanation and consistency check

The PROV holds the edges of the origin (who/what/when generated), and the evidence path is presented when responding; the AIF holds the argument graph of claim - evidence - counterargument, allowing the user to say "why this is so"; and the AIF holds the argument graph of claim - evidence - counterargument, allowing the user to say "why this is so". ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argument_Interchange_ Format?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3) Comparison of representative approaches (to the point)
table:_
Strain Main extraction Structure used Strengths/uses (key points)

GraphRAG (Microsoft) KG extraction with LLM + community detection -> hierarchy summary KG + hierarchy (global/local/DRIFT) Strong overall and multi-document QFS. Full operational guidance and implementation. ([Microsoft GitHub https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Microsoft https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/ blog/graphrag-new-tool-for-complex-data-discovery-now-on-github/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

HippoRAG Entity/Relationship KG + Personalized PageRank Low cost high accuracy with multi-leap QA. Strong even for single-stage acquisition. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

LightRAG Triple Extraction Lightweight KG + K/V index Easy setup, low latency. ([lightrag.github.io https://lightrag.github.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05779?utm_source=chatgpt. com])

LlamaIndex-KG Triplet Extraction Subgraph RAG Easy to configure to add a KG retriever to an existing RAG. ([LlamaIndex https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/api_reference/indices/knowledge_graph/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Theanine Dialogue memory fragments Timeline linked by time and causality Long-term dialogue to understand the "history of change" and reflect it in responses. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996])
RAPTOR Embedded -> Cluster Hierarchical summary tree (Tree/DAG) Search huge corpus step by step from top concepts. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.18059?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

G-Retriever/GRAG graph QA assumption GNN + LLM + RAG Giant graph QA for high speed/high accuracy. ([NeurIPS Proceedings https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/efaf1c9726648c8ba363a5c927440529-Paper-Conference. pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.232.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com]
4) Implementation intuition (design patterns)
(a) Data model design

Property Graph or RDF: Ease of query (Cypher) or standard vocabulary/interoperability (RDF/OWL, PROV-O)? It is easier to attach the source/generation process with PROV from the beginning. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Node type design: `Entity / Event / Claim / Source / Community / Memory`, etc. Time (occurrence / observation / validity period) and causality are primary class citizens.

ID and identification: core reference integration (separate descriptions of the same person/organization). Paying the cost of knowledge maintenance in the initial phase stabilizes multi-jump searches in the later stages.
(b) Extraction pipeline (minimum configuration)
1. segmentation (paragraph/sentence/speech) → language preprocessing (NER, co-ref)

2. relation/event extraction: REBEL/OneIE/DyGIE++ etc. or LLM-guided triad extraction (cost⇆precision tradeoff). ([ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2021.findings-emnlp.204.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [arXiv https://arxiv.org/pdf/1909.03546? utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. time/causality link: extract event time/sequence/causality (rules + LLM or existing methods) ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.09570?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4. normalization/identification (KB link, dictionary, embedding)
5. storage (Graph DB / RDF store) + dual index (vector & graph)

6. (Optional) Hierarchical: GraphRAG community detection -> report generation, pre-calculation of RAPTOR hierarchical summary tree. ([Microsoft https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-new-tool-for-complex-data-discovery-now-on-github/?utm_source= chatgpt.com], [arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.18059?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(c) Manner of Retrieval
Local: seed node from question and neighborhood expansion + source text chunks together (GraphRAG: Local). ([Microsoft GitHub https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Global: synthesis across community summaries (GraphRAG: Global/DRIFT). Works for theme-based questions. ([Microsoft https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-improving-global-search-via-dynamic-community-selection/?utm_ source=chatgpt.com])

Ranking: hybrid PPR/short path/centricity and embedding similarity; PPR is the key to HippoRAG (good starting point for implementation). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(d) Generation
Pass "structure" to the prompt: subgraph (nodes/edges/provenance) + minimal source text.

Hierarchical summary synthesis: GraphRAG's step-by-step synthesis of community report -> partial response -> final summary is less likely to break down even at large scale. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(e) Memory (dialogue/agent)

Theanine style: Present necessary parts from a timeline linked by time and causality without deleting memory. MemGPT/LongMem is supplemented by overflow history storage (hierarchical memory). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996], [NeurIPS Proceedings https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/ebd82705f 44793b6f9ade5a669d0f0bf-Paper-Conference.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(f) Evaluation
QA/Summary: Accuracy (EM/F1), inclusiveness/diversity (e.g., QFS settings for GraphRAG articles). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Memory integration understanding: see if you can really use "past event transitions" with a counterfactual test like Theanine's TeaFarm. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996])
(g) Risks and countermeasures
Extraction illusions: LLM extraction produces false links/over-abstraction. Mitigate by two-step extraction (candidate -> validation) or source-required.

Renewal and Drift: designing incremental renewal of new documents and recalculation strategies for old summaries/communities; GraphRAG adjusts cost/quality by switching between global/local/DRIFT. ([Microsoft https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/introducing-drift-search-combining-global-and-local-search-methods-to- improve-quality-and-efficiency/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
5) First, implementation templates (minimum configuration)
1. base: vector RAG (embedding + preservation of original text).

2. KG Combination: generate and store triples in LlamaIndex KnowledgeGraphIndex (can be Neo4j or RDF). At the same time, PROV-O is used to connect the sources. ([LlamaIndex https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/api_reference/indices/knowledge_graph/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [W3C https://www.w3 .org/TR/prov-overview/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
3. graph utilization:
Local GraphRAG with proximity subgraph + original text. ([Microsoft GitHub https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Pre-calculate community detection -> hierarchical summaries as needed (for global and DRIFT questions). ([Microsoft https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-new-tool-for-complex-data-discovery-now-on-github/?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
If you have a lot of multiple bounces, install HippoRAG's PPR. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
4. dialogue memory: event nodes (utterances/actions/preferences) for each user are linked by time and causality to maintain a timeline (Theanine's policy). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996])
6) Usage guidelines (roughly)
**ask for "big picture/theme "**: GraphRAG (global/DRIFT) or RAPTOR. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

'Multi-jump QA with few clues': HippoRAG (PPR) -> G-Retriever/GRAG if needed. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [NeurIPS Proceedings https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/file/efaf1c9726648c8ba363a5c927440529-Paper-Conference.pdf?utm_ source=chatgpt.com], [ACL Anthology https://aclanthology.org/2025.findings-naacl.232.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

I want to add KG with low operational cost": LightRAG or LlamaIndex-KG. ([lightrag.github.io https://lightrag.github.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [LlamaIndex https ://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/api_reference/indices/knowledge_graph/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

I want to use it without losing the context of the long-term dialogue": theanine time and causal timeline + MemGPT/LongMem as needed. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996], [NeurIPS Proceedings https ://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/ebd82705f44793b6f9ade5a669d0f0bf-Paper-Conference.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com ])
7) Supplement: Graph-of-Thoughts system (graphing of "thoughts")

The target of extraction is not "external text" but LLM intermediate thoughts, but a system that enhances inference with graph structure (reuse, branching, confluence). It can be used in conjunction with external KG for the framework of inference. ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.09687?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Reference and starting point links (excerpts)

GraphRAG (How it works, implementation, and operations blog) ([Microsoft GitHub https://microsoft.github.io/graphrag/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Microsoft https://www. microsoft.com/en-us/research/blog/graphrag-new-tool-for-complex-data-discovery-now-on-github/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
HippoRAG（NeurIPS'24） ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.14831?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
LightRAG ([lightrag.github.io https://lightrag.github.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.05779?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
LlamaIndex: KnowledgeGraphIndex ([LlamaIndex https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/api_reference/indices/knowledge_graph/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Theanine（NAACL'25） ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.10996])

GraphRAG Survey（2024） ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.08921?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Next Steps (Memo for Practical Use)

In PoC: 1) Triplet extraction + Subgraph RAG (inexpensive) → 2) Community summary/DRIFT ("big picture" question support) → 3) PPR (multi-jump reinforcement) → 4) Dialogue timeline (long-term memory), in that order of expansion.
Metrics: mix QA (EM/F1), inclusivity/diversity (QFS systems), counterfactuals (TeaFarm). ([arXiv https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.16130?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Policy: Provnance (source path) on all output. Effective for future audit and observability. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If necessary, the data at hand/requirements (corpus size, question patterns, latency budget) will be fleshed out to a minimum configuration blueprint.

W3C PROV
[GPT5.icon]
You only need to hold the following.
main point

W3C PROV is a family of standards for representing "[provenance]" in a common format. It describes **who** the data or artifact is, **what activity** it went through, and **which entity** it became. It is used for reliability assessment, reproducibility, auditing, and traceability of data systems. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-overview/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Core Concepts (3)
Entity: A "thing/data" at a given point in time.
Activity: Some kind of process or operation (can have a start/end time).
Agent: A person, organization, software, etc., involved in an Activity.
Typical relations: `wasGeneratedBy`, `used`, `wasDerivedFrom`, `wasAttributedTo`, `wasAssociatedWith`, `actedOnBehalfOf`. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Specification Family (Which one do you read/use?)
PROV-PRIMER (Getting Started, This First) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-primer/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
PROV-DM (Definition of Conceptual Model) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-dm/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
PROV-N (human-readable notation) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-n/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
PROV-O (OWL2/RDF ontology, for Linked Data and SPARQL) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
PROV-XML (XML Schema), PROV-AQ (Get History API/Linking Guidelines), PROV-Constraints (Validity Constraints) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-aq/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
PROV-JSON (not a W3C member submission or recommendation, but has examples of use in practice) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/Submission/prov-json/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Mini Example
PROV-N
code:provn
document
prefix ex <http://example.com/>
entity(ex:cleaned_csv)
entity(ex:raw_csv)
agent(ex:alice)
used(ex:cleaning, ex:raw_csv)
wasGeneratedBy(ex:cleaned_csv, ex:cleaning)
wasAssociatedWith(ex:cleaning, ex:alice)
wasAttributedTo(ex:cleaned_csv, ex:alice)
endDocument
(See PROV-N for syntax details; go to PROV-O below if you want to use it in RDF.) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-n/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
PROV-O（Turtle）
code:turtle
@prefix prov: <http://www.w3.org/ns/prov#> .
@prefix ex:   <http://example.com/> .
ex:cleaned_csv a prov:Entity ;
prov:wasGeneratedBy ex:cleaning ;
prov:wasAttributedTo ex:alice .
ex:raw_csv a prov:Entity .
ex:cleaning a prov:Activity ;
prov:used ex:raw_csv ;
prov:startedAtTime "2025-09-01T12:00:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime ;
prov:endedAtTime   "2025-09-01T12:05:00Z"^^xsd:dateTime ;
prov:wasAssociatedWith ex:alice .
ex:alice a prov:Agent .
(See PROV-O for vocabulary and modeling guidelines.) ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Practical Tips

If there is an RDF infrastructure, adopt PROV-O (easy to track and visualize with SPARQL). For lightweight client-to-client exchange, consider PROV-JSON/JSON-LD systems (but with different standard status). ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In the API design, PROV-AQ is used to link from the resource to the coming history and how to get it. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-aq/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If you are aware of consistency checks and logical reasoning, you satisfy the PROV-Constraints rule. ([W3C https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-constraints/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Conversion/verification tools and libraries (e.g. PROV Toolbox for Java) are also available. ([openprovenance.org https://openprovenance.org/service/about.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If necessary, we will also cut together a minimum subset design and **schema (SHACL)** for your data model.

pages.title: Justice and rejection sensitivity in children and adolescents with ADHD symptoms

lines.text: Justice and rejection sensitivity in children and adolescents with ADHD symptoms
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00787-014-0560-9
[GPT5.icon]
Paper abstract (Bondü & Esser, 2015)
Topic: How justice sensitivity (JS) and rejection sensitivity (RS) are related to comorbid problems (depression, behavior problems, low self-esteem) in 10-19 year olds with ADHD tendency.

Subjects/measures: 1,235 German schoolchildren; ADHD symptoms, JS (3 perspectives: victim, observer, and perpetrator), frequency of unfair perception, RS (anxious and angry types), depression, behavior problems, and self-esteem measured by questionnaire.
Key Results:
Participants with ADHD symptoms had higher victim JS, [perception of unfairness], and anxiety/anger RS, and lower perpetrator JS.
Latent variable path analysis showed that JS and RS partially mediate the association between ADHD symptoms → comorbid problems.

Implication: In ADHD support, there is significance in incorporating psychoeducational and CBT interventions (e.g., reevaluation of interpretations, relearning social cues) that work on sensitivity to "unfairness" and sensitivity to rejection. *Causality cannot be determined due to the cross-sectional nature of the study.
Terminology Positioning

Justice Sensitivity (JS): a characteristic of how often one perceives injustice and how strongly one reacts to it. Standard to measure from multiple perspectives of victim/observer/perpetrator. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7868537/])

[Rejection Sensitivity] (RS): the tendency to anticipate rejection anxiously/angry and react strongly (Downey & Feldman model). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8714401/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9768487/?utm _source=chatgpt.com])
Related Research Map (representative examples)

JS x Aggression: victim JS and RS associated with elevated reactive/instrumental aggression, perpetrator JS associated with inhibitory direction. Confirmed in a large sample. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/25136820/])
[Reactive and instrumental aggression]

JS/RS x Depression (longitudinal): youth with higher depression show higher victim JS and (anxiety/angry) RS, an association that persists across time (N=1,665, at time 2). ([Frontiers https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg.2017.01446/full?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28955257/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Interrelationships among multiple "susceptibility" traits: JS, RS, [provocation susceptibility], [moral aversion susceptibility], etc. are bundled and correlated in ego-orientation/other-orientation and linked to [aggression] via hostility attribution bias and anger traits. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4884733/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[Sensitivity to Provocation and Moral Aversion]

ADHD and Social Feedback/RS: Young ADHD tendency is associated with hypersensitivity to [Social Feedback] and self-reported RS (task/neurophysiological indicators). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6395560/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30155685/? utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Measurement development of JS: English adaptation of the simplified JSS-8 (distinguishing between "fundamentalist JS" and "opportunistic JS"). ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10627457/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Reading Points/Practical Tips

Profile asymmetry: important in that it is easy to be "victim JS↑/perpetrator JS↓" in ADHD. Over-detection of injustice and underestimation of the perpetrator of self can occur simultaneously. This is easily connected to peer relationship friction -> depression/behavior problems. ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24878677/])
Intervention Design:

There is a theoretical basis for cognitive reassessment (training not to assume that ambiguous cues = hostility) and rereading of social cues to lower hostility attribution bias and reduce aggression. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4884733/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Responding to RS (monitoring rejection anticipation, attention shifting, strengthening supportive relationships) is effective in secondary prevention of depression/anxiety. ([PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3733267/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Supplemental: Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria (RSD) is a concept widely discussed in party and qualitative research, but it is not a diagnostic name and research accumulation is ongoing. There is a growing body of qualitative data on experiences with and making sense of criticism and rejection. ([PLOS https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0263366&utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm .nih.gov/articles/PMC10569543/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[Justice]
[ADHD]

perception of unfairness
[GPT5.icon]
Perceived injustice / unfairness perception is,

Definition: a subjective perception that an event or treatment is so rated as "unfair and outside of legitimate standards". It refers to "seeming/feeling" that way, rather than whether or not it is actually unfair.
Different from what?
[Justice sensitivity = A personality trait (tendency) to find and react strongly to injustice.
Perceived unfairness = Evaluation of the level of state that occurs in each situation and how often it occurs (how much unfairness do you think you see).
Types of [injustice] covered (4 typical classifications)
1.[Inequity of distribution]: Unjust distribution of results, rewards, and burdens
2.[Procedural unfairness]: The decision-making process and rule operation are unfair.
3. interpersonal (interaction) inequity: [rudeness], prejudice, lack of respect
[Inequity in interpersonal interaction]
[対等でない]、[対等ではない]、[対等に扱われてない]という気持ち[nishio.icon]
4. unfairness of information/explanation: Insufficient or dishonest disclosure of reasons/information
[Inequity of information].
Viewpoint:
Victim's perspective (I'm taking the brunt of it)
Observer's perspective (others are being treated unfairly)
Perpetrator's perspective (I may have done injustice to others)
How to measure (example): on a self-report scale
Likert-graded "I often see/get unfair treatment in my daily life," etc.
How unfair do you feel it is" rating for specific case assumptions (vignettes)

Depending on the field of study, the IEQ (Injustice Experience Questionnaire) in the pain domain and the Organizational Justice in the Workplace (Distribution, Procedures, and Interactions) scale measure proximity concepts.
Related psychological processes:

High perceived unfairness is more likely to be associated with anger, hostility attribution bias, and distrust, and can be associated with whistleblowing and norm-corrective behavior, while increasing the risk of reactive aggression, depression, and stress.
A simple mathematical view (reference):

There is a formulation in the literature that a large discrepancy (e.g., bias in $A/C$) between the actual quantity $A$ obtained and the "quantity you think is reasonable" $C$ is likely to cause unfair perception.

In short, inequity perception is "the evaluation of events" and justice sensitivity is "the trait of ease of evaluation". In research and interventions, it is helpful to separate the two to gain perspective.

Reactive and instrumental attacks
Discussion of splitting [attack] into two types
[GPT5.icon]
terminology
[Reactive aggression: aggression that occurs as an impulsive response to an external stimulus such as provocation, insult, or injustice. Strong anger and high arousal.
[instrumental / proactive aggression: premeditated aggression used as a means to an end (e.g., to gain money, elevate status, control). Anger is not essential.
Typical Differences
Triggers:
Reactive = perceived provocation/threat (likely to involve hostility attribution bias)
Instrumental = expectation of reward and benefit, learned gain
Emotion:
Reactive = anger/frustration↑, impulsivity↑
Instrumental = emotionally flat is acceptable, planning ↑
Time Characteristics:
Reactive = on the spot/short-circuited
Instrumental = preparation and repetition are possible
Example:
Reactive = hit when insulted / pushed away when pushed away
Instrumental = threaten to take money/ bully to ruin reputation
Easily Relevant Factors:
Reactive = difficulty controlling anger, immature emotional regulation, attention bias
Instrumental = reward sensitivity, reduced empathy, antisocial learning
Measurement (representative)
Two dimensions (reactive/instrumental) are evaluated separately, such as RPQ (Reactive-Proactive Aggression Questionnaire).
Direction of intervention (roughly)
Reactive: trigger recognition, anger management, cognitive reappraisal, relearning of social cues.
Instrumental: consistent cost presentation (punishment/loss), learning alternative reward pathways, training in norms/empathy.
The actual behavior is often mixed motives and may not be neatly categorized one way or the other.

lines.text: Sensitivity to provocation and moral aversion
[GPT5.icon]
[Provocation sensitivity

Definition: Tendency to perceive the words and actions of others as provocation (insults and unfair treatment) and to rise to anger and aggressive impulses. Easily associated with reactive aggression and hostility attribution bias. ([SAGE Journals https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1080/02134748.2017.1385241?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [PMC https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih. gov/articles/PMC4522743/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Frontiers https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/psychology/articles/10.3389/fpsyg. 2016.00795/full?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Measurement Representation:

Rejection Sensitivity
[GPT5.icon]
Rejection sensitivity (RS) is a cognitive-emotional trait that makes people anticipate "I might be rejected," hypersensitive to social cues, and prone to overreacting to real or imagined rejection.
contents
Process (typical)
Anxious anticipation: "I will be rejected.
2. hypervigilance: overdetection of ambiguous cues as signs of rejection (attribution of hostility)
Reaction: avoidance, pandering, self-deprecation, or anger → reactive aggression
Subtype
Anxious RS: Atrophy, excessive consideration, testing behavior
Anger-type RS: Damaging Interpretation → Blame, sudden counterattack
Measurement (representative)
RSQ (Rejection Sensitivity Questionnaire) system:
Synthesized and averaged "how anxious" x "how much rejection is anticipated" for each situation (adult version, child version, romantic situation version, etc.).
Different from what?

Attachment anxiety/avoidance: style of overall relationship expectations; RS is oversensitive to situation evaluation; RS is not sensitive to the situation; RS is not sensitive to the situation; RS is not sensitive to the situation.
Justice sensitivity: hypersensitivity to injustice (violation of norms of others); RS is hypersensitive to being rejected by oneself.
Neurotic tendency: general instability of emotions, RS is trigger specific of rejection.
Related Outcomes (Trends)
Internalization: social anxiety, depression, isolation
Externalization: anger, reactive aggression, relational friction
Vicious circle: self-fulfilling loop where behavior caused by fear of rejection leads to actual rejection
It is discussed as an aggravating factor that can amplify interpersonal stress in ADHD and ASD.
Direction of intervention (e.g.)
Training in reevaluating interpretations: don't assume that ambiguous cues = rejection
Attention Bias Modification/Metacognition/Mindfulness
Interpersonal exposure (safe and gradual) and emotional regulation skills (e.g., DBT)
Reduce "uncertainty" by clarifying feedback and developing notice rules (school/workplace)
Terminology note: Difference from RSD

RSD (Rejection Sensitive Dysphoria) is a label for strong distressing experiences used in clinical and party circles, and RS is better developed for academic operationalization and measurement. It is easier to distinguish and organize them according to use.

Harari's NEXUS: A Human History of Information explains that the foundation of the "information network" that drives human society consists of two pillars: "myth (a story that everyone believes)" and "bureaucracy (a mechanism for gathering and processing information).
Myths (stories we all believe)

Narratives that "everyone believes to be true," such as national myths, religions, the value of money, and corporate brands, give legitimacy and unity to the cooperation of large groups of people. For example, the Bible is a collection of stories, but it became "the story that unites society" because it was selected, edited, and distributed by churches.
Bureaucracy (the mechanism for handling information)

The "information infrastructure" of laws, family and census records, tax records, maps, schools, and newspapers keeps track of people and resources and ensures that orders and policies reach the people on the ground. Harari describes the bureaucracy itself as a "huge information network.
The relationship and dilemma between the two

Large societies have always relied on "the power of the myth [of storytelling]" and "the power of the bureaucracy [of practice]," but those who spin the tales and those who manipulate the books often tend to look in different directions. Many institutions, he states, are characterized by what balance they strike between the needs of these two parties.

A bias toward either side is dangerous. If only the narrative gets out of control, it is easy to lean toward [populism] and tyranny, and if only the bureaucracy gets bloated, it is easy to lean toward ruthless and rigid governance - so a self-cleansing (verification, transparency, error correction) mechanism is needed," he suggests.
Connecting to the Now (AI)

The book also warns that AI could become the new "bureaucracy" (information processing mechanism), which could amplify the myth-bureaucracy dynamic. The overall message is to review the relationship between information, myths, and bureaucracy across history.
