pages.title: No One Left Behind and No One Left Behind."

lines.text: No One Left Behind and No One Left Behind."
[GPT5.icon]
Difference in nuance
[no one left behind]
A way of saying active/promise. A nuance in which the actor (government, society, us) pledges not to take any action that will be left undone. It is suitable for slogans and clarifies responsibility.
[No one gets left behind.]
A passive/consequence way of speaking. The "result" of not being left behind is described, and the actor is not indicated. It is suitable for explaining a philosophy or a vision of achievement.
Note that "[none]" is a stronger emphasis than "none" ("not a single person, zero") and increases sloganeering.
Official" notation in Japan

The Japanese government (Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Cabinet Office, etc.) consistently uses the motto "[No one is left behind. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/SDGs/about/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Chiebukuro https://www.chisou.go.jp/tiiki/ kankyo/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In the Japanese version of the 2030 Agenda, the phrase "No one is left behind." is translated as "I pledge that I will not be left behind. However, the former (no one gets left behind) is the established motto. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/sdgs/pdf/000101402.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Guideline for differentiation of use

Measures, declarations and slogans → No one is left behind (showing responsibility and commitment) ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/SDGs/about/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Explanation of the vision of society → A society where no one is left behind (state the state of achievement)

In short, the "official" translation in Japan is "no one will be left behind" (active), and the passive form is sometimes used in the explanatory context of the text. ([Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan https://www.mofa.go.jp/mofaj/gaiko/oda/SDGs/about/index.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

pages.title: A Framework for Constructing Concept Maps from E-Books Using Large Language Models: Challenges and Future Directions

lines.text: A Framework for Constructing Concept Maps from E-Books Using Large Language Models: Challenges and Future Directions
[https://gyazo.com/71b0a04b4c85c210d0158d1d68362415]
A Framework for Constructing Concept Maps from E-Books Using Large Language Models: Challenges and Future Directions
A story about using LLM to create a [conceptual map
https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389522283_A_Framework_for_Constructing_Concept_Maps_from_E-Books_Using_Large_Language_Models_Challenges_and_Future_Directions
[GPT5.icon]

A study that proposed a framework for automatic generation of concept maps from e-books (segmentation → concept extraction → relationship identification → integration) in LLM (GPT-4o), and tested its effectiveness and issues using elementary Python lecture materials.
summary of key points

Background: E-books are not suitable for structured browsing. Concept maps are effective for understanding, memorizing, and navigating, but human creation is expensive; LLM aims to automate this process.
Framework:

1. sectioning of chapters and sections → 2) extraction of key concepts in each section → 3) identification of relationships among concepts (e.g., hierarchical relationships) → 4) overall integration into a concept map (directed graph).

Difference from related studies: conventional TF-IDF/LDA/cooccurrence/knowledge base utilization is task fragmented. The proposal uses LLM for consistent processing and contextual understanding to suppress semantic drift.
Assessment data: 12 lectures of the university's "Introduction to Python" (electronic materials).
Main results:
Sectional split: 57 sections in total, 10/12 lectures in perfect agreement (average 4.75 sections/lecture).

Concept extraction: 138 GPT-generated concepts vs. 111 teacher GT concepts; Precision 0.80 / Recall 0.86 / F1 0.83. Complete coverage of GT in 6/12. Additional 27 concepts (many useful), 18 missing (may be absorbed in hierarchies or paraphrases).

Relation identification: 154 hierarchical relations, 70 others; hierarchies are generally appropriate, but relations with little semantic value are mixed in. Suggested that constrained generation is effective.
Generated maps prioritize conceptual logic over teacher sequencing order. Provides another perspective on learning and understanding.
Issue:
Inconsistency with educational goals (mixing peripheral concepts).
Optimization of human intervention (human-in-the-loop burden).
Hallucinations (especially non-hierarchical relationships). Mitigated by choice constraints, etc.
Future:
Domain adaptation/fine-tuning to align with educational design.
Concept stratification (core/auxiliary/developmental) and expansion.
Co-generated by role-sharing agents (administrators, domain experts, and data engineers).
E-book system integration (relationship discovery and dashboarding with interactive navigation, user feedback, and learning logs).
Conclusion.

LLM is promising for automatic concept map generation (especially hierarchical structure), but educational goal alignment, relationship quality control, and human intervention design are key. Validation with large-scale data and other LLMs is the next step.

event notes
[GPT5.icon]
The following is an "abstract version for anyone to read" (proper names and media are omitted).
What happened (abstraction)
1. in an open communal space, a participant posts a lengthy, professional proposal and commentary.
2. another participant shares procedural information to the effect that "proposals are no longer being accepted".
3. further operational advice (threading, volume considerations, etc.) will be provided.
4. the first participant took it as a **point from above (relational frame)** and reacted with strong language.
5. the management publicly cautions and requests compliance with the Code.
6. the parties argue unfairness in terms of undue consideration of context and reasonable care.
7. a third party adds empathy, supplementation, and another point of view, and the issue shifts from **"pros and cons of the content" to "operation and consideration of the place "**.
8. the operational decision was ultimately upheld and the norms were confirmed, but the friction in the relationship remained.
General principles that worked behind the scenes
Common ground of attention: readability of public space is a common resource. Long and individual repartee leads to wear and tear, and norms are triggered.
Lack of explicit norms: If the rules are unclear, procedural unfairness is likely to occur.
Intent ≠ Impact: Even well-intentioned advice can create a backlash if taken as a relational message.
Sensitivity mismatch: If sensitivity to rejection or provocation is high, ambiguous pointers are over-detected as aggression/rejection, leading to reactive aggression.
Legitimacy of sanctions depends on procedures: public attention has high face costs, and proportionality, sequence, and clarity of explanation determine acceptability.
Summary in one line

The clash between "freedom of individual expression" and "legibility of the place and procedural fairness" turned into a public escalation due to the meshing of relational frames and sensitivities - an event.
[GPT5.icon]
1) [Attention Commons
Readability and tracking costs of public channels are resources shared by participants.
Long sentences, digressions, and individual repartee are perceived as excessive consumption of attentional resources, and norms (threading and shortening) are invoked.
→ Distributive justice tradeoff of "[individual freedom of expression]" vs.
2) [Conflict between explicit and implicit norms].
When the rules are unclear (the extent of "chit-chat, etc."), parties are more likely to perceive procedural unfairness.
Management refers to implicit norms as "overall optimal practices"; parties demand explicit statements.
→ Lack of visualization of rules amplifies unfair perception.
3) Estimation of [relationship frame] (status/solidarity)
The same content can cause a backlash as a threat to self-esteem and autonomy if the expression is read in a higher -> lower frame (e.g., "supplement for ~").
→ Speech has a dual message of "content (what)" and "relationship (how/standing)" (theory of [face]).
4) Susceptibility dynamics (RS x provocation sensitivity x JS)
The side with higher [rejection sensitivity] (RS) is more likely to overdetect ambiguous attention as a rejection signal.
If the recipient has a sensitivity to provocation, it is easy to take a deviation from the norm as a provocation and choose a stronger reciprocation.
When the perception of unfairness stands on both sides, reactive attacks and justifications are looped.
→ The meshing of "susceptibility vectors" creates an escalation circuit.
5) Discrepancy between Intent and Impact (Intent ≠ Impact)
Even a well-intentioned supplement or general caution will be evaluated according to how it is received by the recipient.
Load estimates and tones are hypersensitive in public spaces.
→ Misread rate is approximately Misread ∝ (Ambiguity x Sensitivity x Openness) / Norm Clarity
6) Legitimacy of sanctions = Procedural Justice
The proportionality and accountability of the ladder of intervention (private letter -> thread guidance -> public attention) determines the level of acceptance.
Direct public warnings have a high [face cost] and can easily turn into a backlash -> legitimacy dispute.
→ Even the same conclusion can be convinced by "order and transparency".
7) Reputation games in public space
Mutual criticism in public can easily turn into a [reputation game] that assumes a third-party audience.
When one side goes into character evaluation, the other side responds with rules and rights discourse (consideration and law), splitting the issue into "procedure vs. character.
→ Hierarchy shifted from agenda to meta agenda (operational justification).
8) Binomial tension between inclusion and discipline
Inclusion (reasonable accommodation) and field discipline (uniform operation) cannot be maximized simultaneously.
Principle: **Designs that align "same participation opportunities "** rather than "same outcomes".
→ The formulation that "individual adjustment is not an "exemption" but a "change of method" reduces conflicts.
Typical causal patterns (abstract causal diagram, text version)
1. ambiguity of norms x tight attention-sharing land
2. → Third party relationship frame stronger point
3. → Receiver's RS activated (over-detection of rejection)
4. → Reactive aggression (shift from content to critique of the relationship)
5. → Public sanction by management (proportionality/sequencing in dispute)
6. → Amplified perceptions of procedural unfairness/inequity on both sides
7. → Expand to meta agenda (legitimacy, consideration, rights)
Abstract rule (the smallest set reducible to operation)
R1: Write content and relationships separately (I-message + concrete action suggestions).
R2: Intervention is private communication priority -> minimally publicized as necessary (proportionality, clear reasons).
R3: Preliminary "Norms for Attention Sharing Places" fixed display with short text (assumed post/thread criteria).
R4: Institutionalize consideration as an adjustment of means, not an exemption of results (application window and SLA).
**R5: Avoid personality assessment and limit feedback to actions, procedures, and locations.
If we drop to this 8 principles + 5 rules, frictions like this one can be easily reproduced and verified as where the cognition was misaligned/which procedures were missing before "who is right".

pages.title: Parable of the left-hand side of the road

[GPT5.icon][nishio.icon]
Compare with "[No need to prioritize people who can't use a phone or computer.
Differences in the assumed image of the parties involved
This is [willingness not to participate in the procedure] (will not) / [who will not].
[We must avoid the confusion of "I can't" and "I won't".
→[I think that] people who say they can't do something without a clear reason are the ones who won't do it."]
Difference in meaning of "nothing."
B: No special handling, but overall load is reduced by digitization and existing contact points are maintained → resulting in shorter waiting time for non-digital layer (indirect benefit).
A: Lower priority is given to requests outside the queue. Processing resources are first directed to P in the queue, and if there is room, to Q as well.
→ B's "do nothing" = benefit from baseline maintenance + externalities; A's "do nothing" = priority allocation issue.
justification
B: [Pareto improvement] (spillover effect of overall efficiency improvement) + [continuation of existing procedures] to ensure "not truncation".
A: [Procedural justice] (fairness on a first-come, first-served, procedural order) + justification for the allocation of limited resources.
Organizing framework (2 x 2)
Ability × Willingness
Can x do = digital row (highest priority)
Cannot x Do = Analog column (non-digital layer of B: baseline maintenance + indirect benefits)
Can do x won't do = Q in A (low priority)
Can't do x won't do = Minimal response after identifying factors (system awareness, guidance on alternative measures, etc.)
Practical and Representational Implications
Add a sentence to A: "'Do nothing' means no special treatment; maintain a baseline window, create extra capacity through overall efficiency, and provide assistance as needed."
No need to align with the same content, the second half feels too much like B, only the first half should be adopted.[nishio.icon]
B's argument can be internalized into A's framework (resource allocation = column priority, and externalities shorten non-digital columns as well).

pages.title: If someone says they can't do something without a clear reason, they're probably someone who won't do it.

lines.text: If someone says they can't do something without a clear reason, they're probably someone who won't do it.
[nishio.icon]If you're saying you can't do something when no clear reason for not doing it exists, you're the one who won't do it.
[GPT5.icon]The short answer is that in terms of behavior, "it is true, but not always so." Placing an axis of distinction improves the outlook.
1) Can't vs. won't (4 quadrants)
Objective constraints x Willingness: Lack of tools, time, skills, and procedural information (= a legitimate example of "I can't do it")
Subjective Constraint x Willing: anxiety, risk perception, poor executive functioning, unverbalized friction (difficult to see as a "clear reason" from the outside)
Strategic speech x No intention: Aiming for special treatment, saying "I can't" (in reality, "I won't")
Preference x No intention: not rationally chosen on a cost-effective basis ("don't do it")
Many cases that appear to the observer to be "no clear reason" fall into (2) ([invisible costs]). Confusing this area with (3) and (4) can lead to misallocation and flame wars.
I see[nishio.icon]
2) Operational judgment (by procedure, not by label)
1. present a minimum support set
Clarification of procedures, presentation of time required, one-click, alternative channels, accompanied assistance for a short time, etc. (low-cost and high-effectiveness).
2. even if the observable resources are supplemented, it will not move → treat it as "not done" in terms of action (lower priority).
3. move after completion → considered to have been "not possible" (to be incorporated into the standard support thereafter).

[Judging by behavior] allows for fair operation without relying on the person's innermost feelings or confession (also consistent with the "line up = order of procedure" principle of "[those who don't stand in line]").
Related: [Judging by actions, not words].
3) Distribution and Communication Guidelines
Procedural fairness: those who meet the columns (requirements) are processed first.
Baseline maintenance + externalities: overall efficiency gains create extra capacity, and the non-digital layer also has shorter waiting times (discussion point B).
Only low-cost reasonable accommodations should be standardized (e.g., substitute entry of in-person appointments, continuation of paper forms, etc.).

The expression is more of a requirement statement than a reason pry: "If you follow this procedure, it will take you XX minutes. If it's too difficult, we'll provide Y. If it still doesn't work, go to the **"If you can spare the time, we'll do it" box**.
4) One-line summary
It is safe and fair to treat "I can't" without a clear reason as "I won't" only when no action is taken even after minimal support is provided. safe and fair.

There is no need to give "priority" and "special treatment" to those who cannot use a cell phone or computer.
[GPT5.icon]
1) Percentage of work that can be digitized (institutional and possibility-based)
Japan as a whole (based on type of national and local government procedures)

About 50-55% of the documents can be put online (all-inclusive survey in FY2024: 51.6% of 75,071 types online). ([Digital Agency https://www.digital.go.jp/assets/contents/node/basic_page/field_ref_resources/578b4dd0-db54-44da-9850-d76a6248c27f/628232ad /20250804_private-business-dx_outline_02.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

lines.text: Put the first big stone in.
It's a common metaphor, so I'll generate it later.
[GPT5.icon]
A typical "Big Rocks" story goes like this.
1. demonstration in class/training
The instructor prepares a clear glass jar and (1) a large stone, (2) a pebble, and (3) sand (some versions use (4) water).
First, the "big stone" is placed in a jar. It looks full.
Next, put a "pebble" in and shake it, it goes into the gap and still goes in.
And when more "sand" is added, more goes in.
(In the pouring version) water also enters at the end.
2. questions from the lecturer
What is the lesson of this experiment?"
Students tend to answer, "You can get a lot in depending on how you pack it," but the instructor corrects them.
3. the real lesson

'What I really want to tell you is that if you don't put the big stones (the most important things) in first, you won't be able to put them in later.' If you fill it with small errands (pebbles/sand) first, you can't put in the important stuff."
4. correspondence of interpretations
Bottle = my time, attention, and resources (24 hours a day or operating this month).
Large stones = most important tasks directly related to value/goals (family time, deep work, health, etc.).
Pebbles = necessary but less important task.
Sand and water = chore, notification, and inertia.
5. attention to common misunderstandings
This is not "all-in magic". If there are too many big rocks, they won't fit. It is essential to narrow down the number first and place the scheduled blocks first (put them on the calendar first).
To drop it into practice, the standard usage is "decide on up to three large stones for the week and reserve time first → place the remaining pebbles/sand around them".
[GPT5.icon]
The oldest verifiable source in print is "[First Things First]" (1994) by [Stephen R. Covey] et al. In the same book, the "Big Rocks" demonstration story is used.
It was later widely disseminated through FranklinCovey's training materials and videos (a.k.a. "Big Rocks").

Super Bullet Points
>[mr_grayhair https://x.com/mr_grayhair/status/1964917581191762369] NG words in presentations to be aware of
> From Mr. Sugino's "Super Bullet Points" from A.T. Kearney
> https://amzn.to/49dNcgQ
Figure 45: NG words in presentations
Improve ~."
It's not working, so it's only natural to improve.
It is not the improvement itself, but how it is to be improved that is meaningless unless you tell them how to improve.
Reviewing the ~."
It's not working, so it's only natural to revisit it.
It doesn't make sense if you don't tell them how you're going to review it.
"to promote..."
It's natural to promote what you know you're going to do.
It doesn't make sense if you don't tell them what exactly you're going to do.
Optimize ~."
If you can optimize, you do. No one wants to optimize.
It doesn't make sense if you don't tell them what exactly they need to do to optimize.
Balance the ~."
This is the same as "optimize ~." Balancing is a given.
It makes no sense if you don't tell them what happens and what they need to do to achieve a balanced state.
I'll make sure ~ is done thoroughly."
If you can be thorough, you should be.
It is meaningless if you don't tell them specifically how to be thorough.
"to enhance."
⇒This is the same as "be thorough with ~". If you can reinforce it, you do it.
⇒It is meaningless if you don't tell them specifically how you will strengthen it.
"I'm going to do it."
⇒It is natural to do what you are doing or what you are supposed to do.
⇒It is meaningless unless you tell them what you are going to do specifically, not just what you are going to do.

lines.text: Lowering the hurdle to speak reduces the attrition per statement.
from  [Diary 2025-08-28]
Lowering the hurdle to speak reduces the attrition per statement.
When [the hurdle to speak up] is high, 10 out of 100 people speak up and 90 remain silent.
Lowering the hurdle will get 90 out of 100 people to speak up.
In this case, the amount of statements is multiplied by 9, so if the receiver remains the same, the attention per statement is 1/9
[Attention is a scarce resource]
From the point of view of those who originally spoke out, the number has decreased from 9 to 1.
From those who did not speak up, the number is increasing by [0 to 1].
[attention] is [Rare resources], which makes it impossible to lower the hurdle in the first place.
As a result, the opinions of those who speak out without regard to cost appear larger than they really are.
There is no guarantee that those with the loudest voices are the majority.
So it is possible that following the opinions of those with the loudest voices can bring disadvantages to more people
[noisy minority]
Also, people with loud voices may start fights with each other.
The more extreme the views, the more likely they are to speak out, the more divisive they become.
There is an approach that lowers the hurdle by assuming that the AI compresses the data instead of a human reading it directly.
It is assumed that humans do not read what is gathered
Compression by AI always discards some information.
For example, abandoning emotions.

The voice effect refers to the phenomenon in which simply being able to express one's opinion before a decision is made increases [a sense of conviction], [a sense of fairness], [trust], and [willingness to cooperate], regardless of whether or not one agrees with the final outcome. It is used in research on administrative participation, voice systems within organizations, and labor-management relations.

The mechanism is explained as an increase in [procedural justice] and [self-efficacy] of being "listened to/respected," and token participation (venting) and absence of feedback can be counterproductive.
Talking and Feeling Fairness - What Procedural Justice Research Shows Us - Ikuo Sugawara [PDF https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jsl/2013/78/2013_154/_pdf/- char/en]

> In the early studies, comparative studies between procedures were conducted based on the differences in the structure of procedures, such as whether the parties or the judges submit the claims and evidence under the concept of procedural control.
>2 From Fairness Theory to Human Relations Theory

>This procedural justice research has led to studies that have shown the influence of a sense of fairness on people's attitudes and behaviors, but it has also led to an investigation into the causes of such influences.

>In the original procedural justice research, the explanation was that it is still the outcome that people ultimately focus on, and that the reason that party-based procedures feel fair is because they reserve control over the outcome they obtain to make it more favorable to themselves. ...

> However, Lind and Tyler, who subsequently confirmed many procedural justice effects, pointed out that some procedural justice effects, such as "[voice effects]" independent of the outcome (Lind et al. 1990), existed. (Lind et al. 1990), and unlike the original explanation of procedural justice research, it focuses on the procedure itself, not on the influence on the outcome, and points out the importance of the human factor with the authority figure who makes the judgment, or in the case of a trial, with the judge. ...

> One of the characteristics of Lind and Tyler's theory is that it explains procedural justice effects in terms of human relations among those involved in the proceedings, while the structural elements of the proceedings, as in previous studies, are absent.

Core assertion: The union has
1. the face of monopoly (wage premium = squeeze on corporate profits) and,
2.[Collective Voice]/Face of Institutional Responsiveness (collect dissatisfaction and findings and convey them to management through the system)
There are two aspects. The latter can contribute to efficiency through information sharing and the development of procedures.

Key Evidence: Unions reduce turnover and increase length of service. This effect cannot be explained by wages and benefits alone, and the contribution of the voice function is estimated. ([NBER https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w11410/w11410.pdf])

Corporate performance: profit margins consistently declined (wage increases transferred excess profit). Productivity is mixed positive and negative, depending on the environment, with a subsequent review showing average near zero. ([NBER https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w11410/w11410.pdf], [EconStor https://www.econstor.eu/bitstream/10419/20131/1 /dp892.pdf])

Conclusion (later self-evaluation): Summarizes that the decline of unions is a social loss because the "positive effects of Voice" outweigh the "negative effects of monopoly. However, it also positions the design of a non-union type Voice system as important. ([NBER https://www.nber.org/system/files/working_papers/w11410/w11410.pdf])
Supplement: This framework is an application of Hirschman's "Exit-Voice-Loyalty" to the workplace (also explicit in the text).

Reference: 1979 "Two Faces of Unionism" (The Public Interest/text PDF), 1984 book, Freeman (2005) reassessment paper, Hirsch (2003) performance verification. pages.title: Coordinating perceptually grounded categories through language: A case study for colour

lines.text: Coordinating perceptually grounded categories through language: A case study for colour
[GPT5.icon]

The BBS target paper Steels & Belpaeme (2005) "Coordinating perceptually grounded categories through language: a case study for colour "The main points of the paper are compactly summarized in the following order: design (model), experiment, indicators, results, and implications.

BBS (Behavioral and Brain Sciences) "target papers" are the central papers that are the "target" of Open Peer Commentary. Papers on highly important and controversial topics are selected, and a series of short comments from experts (approximately 20 to 40 comments) are published, followed by the author's overall reply at the end.
What is the paper about?

Using color as the subject matter, we examine "how perceptual categories possessed by individuals are sufficiently shared in a group to be communicated in language. Computational models are created for each candidate position (innate/empiricist/culturalist) and compared to see which one is sufficient for sharing. Published in Behavioral and Brain Sciences 28(4), pp. 469-489 (with open peer commentary). ([PubMed https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/16209771/?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [Cambridge University Press & Assessment https://www. cambridge.org/core/journals/behavioral-and-brain-sciences/article/coordinating-perceptually-grounded-categories-through-language-a -case-study-for-colour/423FB60CE8E6BFB0ADC23FFD48FBD4F0?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Model design (3 systems)

[Nativism: Genetic evolutionary model. Examines whether individuals with color categories (prototype groups) as "color genes" converge to sharing through generational change. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])

[empiricism] (Empiricism): individual learning model, where inputs in CIE L*a*b* space are clustered (prototype + fuzzy boundary) in an adaptive network of RBF systems, each of which independently acquires categories. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])

[Culturalism: [Language Games] combine category formation and word adoption in a bidirectional manner (reinforcing successfully transferred categories and words). This allows for simultaneous intra-individual learning and word alignment. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
Experimental Tasks and Data
Discrimination game: The listener identifies the object to which the speaker refers in the presentation set.
Language game (naming): communicated using category ↔ word correspondence. Weight update with success/failure. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
Environment:
1. Munsell 1269 color spectral reflection (380-800nm) → XYZ → L*a*b* conversion (reflects human color vision model).

2. "Realistic statistical distribution" data sampled from 25,000 pixels each from natural and urban landscapes, random Munsell for comparison.([rangev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
indicator
Discriminative success
Communicative success

Consistency is quantified by category variance (category variance; the deviation of categories among individuals) and inter-population variance (inter-population variance). ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
Main Results (Conclusions)
1. individual learning alone "makes each individual better, but sharing is not enough"

Discrimination success reaches almost 100%, but categories are not aligned among individuals (category variance remains). = Solutions are not uniquely determined for the same environment and the same physiology. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
Individual learning alone does not generate a common language system.[nishio.icon]
2. genetic evolution aligns within a population, but "slowly"

Over generations, categories become more consistent (dispersal → low) within the population. However, timescales for adaptation are long (multi-generational). ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
3. fast and highly accurate alignment when there is cultural interaction through language

When category formation and word adoption are combined in a language game, discrimination and transfer success increases simultaneously (transfer success goes up to ≈90%). = Causal influence of language on category acquisition. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
4. environmental statistics alone are not enough to share

Actual nature/urban statistics tend to increase the degree of sharing, but they do not lead to sufficient consistency by themselves. = Three factors are needed: physical (physiology) x environmental statistics x language negotiation. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
Implications (symbolic foundations/universal vs. relative)

For the chicken-and-egg problem (category first or word first), we present a dynamic explanation that bi-directional binding (category ⇄ word) drives alignment. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])

Although universalism (physiological and environmental constraints) alone produces certain trends, linguistic interaction decisively boosts the degree of sharing. However, color is a special domain, and BBS commenters have presented criticisms such as "overemphasizing the influence of language" (e.g., Wachtler et al., Harnad). ([Artificial Intelligence Lab Brussels https://ai.vub.ac.be/sites/default/files/steels-05e.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com], [eprints.soton. ac.uk https://eprints.soton.ac.uk/260503/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Summary (one line)

Social sharing of perceptual categories is made not only by body and environmental statistics, but also by the dynamics of linguistic interactions (cultural negotiation) -- a paper that shows this computationally and experimentally in the color case. ([langev.com https://langev.com/pdf/steels_BBS_color.pdf])
What does "language games interactively combine category formation and word adoption" mean?[nishio.icon]
[GPT5.icon]
In short** "category learning" and "vocabulary learning" are to be updated simultaneously with the success or failure of the same interaction (language game).

Instead of one-way (category -> word pasting only), the way a word is used pushes category boundaries, and at the same time the way the category is held determines the selection and invention of words**--this mutual traction is called "two-way coupling " is called "two-way coupling.
1) What happens in one language game (minimum steps)
1. situational presentation: multiple color chips (context) + speaker chooses one "topic".
2. conceptualization (category side → word):
The speaker selects a discriminative category from his/her perceptual category group (if not, the category is split/adjusted to create one).
If there is an existing word in the category, select it. If not, invent a word and assign it.
3. interpretation (word → category side):
The listener explores the word → (his/her) candidate category, and then applies and points to what can be discriminated in context.
If it fails, adjust/new your own category, and word-category merging is also updated by adopting/weakening it.
4. update (bidirectional):
Success: strengthens the union of its word ⇄ category, suppresses competing words and categories (side suppression). Category center and spread are also fine-tuned.
Failure:
Repair on the lexical side: adopt new words, weaken/remove erroneous word-category combinations.
Repair on the category side: boundary transfer, division/annexation, updating the prototype (to make it discriminable).
The key point is to update both "word combination weights" and "category forms (prototypes and boundaries)" with the same error signal of success or failure.
2) What is "bidirectional" (direction of causation)?
Language → Category: The pressure to get the word through successfully pushes (subdivides and moves) category boundaries to the necessary granularity.
Category → Language: the category structure at hand determines which words are chosen / new words are invented.
3) Formal image (simplified)
Strength of lexical binding [$ \sigma(w,c)]:
Success: [$ \sigma \leftarrow \sigma + \alpha(1-\sigma)] (enhanced)
Failure: [$ \sigma \leftarrow (1-\beta)\sigma] (weakened)
Category prototype [$ p_c] and spread [$ \tau_c]:
On success, fine-tuning toward the topic sample; on failure, firing repairs such as splitting/shifting boundaries, etc.
(*Specific expressions vary by implementation, but both are driven by the same success/failure.)
4) Why it works (Consequences)
Because discrimination (category-side objective) and transfer success (lexical-side objective) are simultaneously optimized in a single iterative game,
Within individuals, words and categories mesh,
Within a group, vocabulary and boundaries converge (convention formation) through interaction.
5) Mini Example
Initial: "red" is too wide and fails to pick up the neighboring vermilion color as well.
The listener dichotomizes the category (red/red) and the speaker invents "vermillion" OR narrows the range of "red".
Subsequent successes strengthen and stabilize "red" ⇄ red and "vermillion" ⇄ vermillion.
In short, the design updates both sides of a word⇄category with the success or failure of a single exchange - this is "binding in both directions".

Capillary suspension
[https://gyazo.com/7c008536b97175fa7388259c5e3789fa]
https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Three-phase-air-liquid-solid-and-two-phase-liquid-solid-regimes-of-a-particulate-ensemble_fig1_250161475
[GPT5.icon]

Capillary suspension is a system in which a very small amount of a "second liquid" (a liquid that does not mix with the main liquid) is added to a suspension containing dispersed particles to form a strong network of particles throughout the sample by forming capillary bridges between the particles, which greatly increases viscosity and yield stress. This is a system in which the viscosity and yield stress increase significantly.
Mechanism: The second liquid cross-links the particles and attracts them to each other by **capillary force (determined by surface tension and wettability)**.
2 states:
Pendula state (second liquid wets particles well) → inter-particle bridging.
Capillary state (hard to wet) → cluster of particles surrounds the second droplet.
Characteristics: Significantly adjusts rheology when added in minute amounts, reversible in shear, and improves sedimentation inhibition and shape retention.
Applications: Ceramic pastes, food products, paints and inks, 3D printing materials, etc.
[nishio.icon]Interpreted as a Plurality-like metaphor
[GPT5.icon]The following is an interpretation of "capillary suspension" read as a metaphor for plurality (⿻).
Correspondence (metaphor)
Particles → diverse actors/communities/fragments of knowledge
Main Liquid → Miscellaneous flows in existing public spaces (SNS, autonomy, markets, etc.)
Second liquid (trace/non-miscible) -> neutral **"bridging medium "** (common API, conventions, rituals, small common budget, translation/summary, visualization tools, etc.)
Capillary force (surface tension x wettability) → inducement x trust congruence (strength of motive to participate and norm conformity)
Contact angle → How well the bridging medium "fits" into each community (acceptance)
Yield stress (force to maintain shape) → minimum cost to maintain the shape of the public sphere (tenacity to keep decisions from collapsing)
Shear → Re-form → Temporarily fluidized by debates, elections, crises → Re-organize after convergence
Analogy between the two states
Pendula state: a small amount of bridging media connects the dots directly (cross-border dialogue, mutual review, co-authorship, mixed teams). = bridging social capital
Capillary state: many parties surround a drop of medium (periphery gathers around a common data set, common fund, common infrastructure). = commons-centered aggregation
Product/Institutional Design Implications
1. very small amounts for big effects: scatter small common objects (protocols, visualization, small grants) rather than huge integration devices.
2. design "wettability": translation, summary, reply control, and code of conduct to make participation easier for everyone (contact angle ↓).
3. avoid over-cohesion: too much media leads to rigidity (factional fixation). Distribute multiple light interventions.
4. cycle design: search phase (fluidization) → summary/consensus building (gelation) → evaluation and re-fluidization rhythm.
5. bridges at critical points: Insert **small bridges (joint facts, common KPIs, shared dashboards)** at the "narrow gaps" of disputes and divisions.
6. diverse drops: juxtapose multiple bridging media (rituals, data, funds, APIs) rather than a single style to lower vulnerability.
Failure Patterns (Caution)
A medium that only gets wet on one side: favors only one side and rejects the other → polarized reinforcement.
Excessive surface tension: too strong inducement for formal entrainment → reduced creativity.
Single medium dependence: network collapse if that medium is lost.
one phrase
By simply scattering a small amount of neutral "second media," fragmented diversity is spontaneously organized into a bridging network.

From this perspective, the implementation of Plurality will be much easier to design if we place policing/broad listening summaries, visualization, posting design, small common funds, interface standards (ID/data API), etc. as "capillary bridges.

LightRAG
[GPT5.icon]

LightRAG is the fastest implementation to try "RAG while graphing and visualizing". It is also suitable for visualization of a book. The following is a summary of LightRAG in the following order: Why LightRAG is suitable for this project → Procedure for immediate use → Specific workflow for a book → Where to get stuck.
Why LightRAG is fit for purpose (key points)

Server with Web UI: Import documents, explore and visualize knowledge graphs, and perform simple RAG queries from a browser (Ollama compatible API included). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

Citation (source) function: allows users to trace evidence by stringing it to a file path or other source (reflected in the design of both the server UI and core). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Multi-format import: PDF / DOC / PPT / CSV / TXT via `textract ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

Storage flexibility: in addition to the default (NetworkX, JSON-based), it is scalable to production-oriented configurations such as Neo4j, PostgreSQL + pgvector/AGE, Milvus/Qdrant/FAISS, etc. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

The model operation intuition is clearly stated: strong LLM for extraction (approx. 32B class, long text support), `BAAI/bge-m3` or `text-embedding-3-large` is recommended for embedding, mix mode is recommended when relanker is enabled, etc. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Shortest setup (touched by Web UI)
1. installation (server version)
code:bash
pip install "lightrag-hku[api]"
cp env.example .env
lightrag-server
After launching, access the Web UI from a browser (UI allows for grabbing/graph visualization/querying). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

Tip: There are reports of cases where PyPI dependencies are not fully inserted automatically. Please install additional dependencies such as `openai`, `transformers`, `ollama`, `nano_vectordb`, etc. as needed. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/333?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
2. main configuration points for .env
LLM: OpenAI (API key) or Ollama (local). Stronger models are recommended for extraction (e.g. GPT-4o series, Llama3.1-70B / Qwen2.5-32B for local). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Embedding: `BAAI/bge-m3` or `text-embedding-3-large` (important to use the same model for indexing and searching). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Storage: default (file + NetworkX) at first, move to Neo4j, etc. when scale increases. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Workflow to visualize one book (for practical use)
Goal: To have a graphical understanding of the chapter structure and keywords/relationships, and to be able to click through to the rationale for the corresponding page.
1) Book preprocessing
Convert PDF to text in pages (or paragraphs). Add a page label such as `book-title | p.12` at the beginning of the text for easy citation as the page source later.
LightRAG can also be imported directly from PDF (`textract`). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
2) Indexing
Upload from Index in Web UI (or API/core).

Entities and relations are extracted during the capture, and a knowledge graph and vector index are created (extraction quality is LLM-dependent; strong models are recommended). (LLM dependent on extraction quality, strong model recommended). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
3) Visualization (Graph)

Web UI Graph allows node search, neighborhood expansion, layout switching, etc. It provides a bird's eye view of the connections between people/concepts/relationships/chapters in a book. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

In addition, the LightRAG GUI made by Streamlit allows you to "insert, query, visualize, and download" (export and create your own views with Cytoscape.js, etc. if needed). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
4) Question (RAG query)
Global/mix is for the big picture of the book, local is for the details. When relanker is enabled, mix is recommended by default. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Turn on citation (source) to see which file (page) it is based on along with the answer. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Minimum script to include per page (if necessary)
Web UI is sufficient, but if you want to keep the page source strictly, use the core to assign an ID to each page and submit it.
code:python
# Follow official initialization procedure: initialize_storages() and initialize_pipeline_status() are required
import asyncio, pdfplumber
from lightrag import LightRAG, QueryParam
from lightrag.llm.openai import gpt_4o_mini_complete, openai_embed
from lightrag.kg.shared_storage import initialize_pipeline_status
WORKDIR = "./book_kg"
async def main():
rag = LightRAG(working_dir=WORKDIR,
embedding_func=openai_embed,
llm_model_func=gpt_4o_mini_complete)
await rag.initialize_storages()
await initialize_pipeline_status()
texts, ids = [], []
with pdfplumber.open("book.pdf") as pdf:
for i, page in enumerate(pdf.pages, start=1):
txt = page.extract_text() or ""
texts.append(f"[page={i}]\n{txt}")
ids.append(f "book#p{i}") # Fix page IDs for easy citation later
await rag.ainsert(texts, ids=ids)
# Example: Big picture query
ans = await rag.aquery("Summarize the core concepts and interrelationships of this book", param=QueryParam(mode="mix"))
print(ans)
asyncio.run(main())
The two initialization steps (`initialize_storages()` and `initialize_pipeline_status()`) are required. If not executed, an error will occur. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Direct PDF import is also possible with `textract`. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Recommended settings (assuming Japanese book)

Embedding: `BAAI/bge-m3` (multilingual) or `text-embedding-3-large` (high precision) is unified in indexing and searching. If you change it in the middle, regenerate the corresponding tables and data directories. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
LLM (extraction): Stronger model (approx. 32B class, long-text support). Llama3.1-70B / Qwen2.5-32B via Ollama for local, GPT-4o series for cloud, etc. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Reranker: enable `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` etc. and make mix mode the default. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
Storage: Default is sufficient for a single book. If you expect corpus expansion, move to Neo4j (KG) + pgvector (vector) in stages. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
A common place to get hooked.

Dependencies do not come in automatically: if there is a shortage in the PyPI version of `lightrag-hku` / `lightrag`, add `openai`, `transformers`, `ollama`, `nano_vectordb`, etc. by hand. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/333?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Embedding was changed in the middle of the process: the same Embedding is assumed for indexing and searching. Rebuild related vector tables/data when changing. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

Graph of UI: There is an announcement that the Graph Viewer of the Web UI is being improved sequentially (functionality is provided). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/685?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Mini procedures to start immediately (1 book)
1. `pip install "lightrag-hku[api]"` → edit `.env` (LLM, Embedding, Storage) → `lightrag-server`. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
2. submit PDFs in the Index of the Web UI (or submit them in page units in preprocessing). ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])
3. search for the main node (concept/person) in the Graph tab → expand the neighborhood → check the page with the source link. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

4. in mix mode, ask questions such as "What is the spine of this book?", "What is the relationship between the main concepts?", "What are the opposite concepts?" and other questions. ([GitHub https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG])

lines.text: It's not a job for humans.
Phrases that software engineers inadvertently use and are interpreted by people of a different culture as strong occupational discrimination and don't
To put it more moderately, it's like, "I think that can be handled more efficiently with a computer."
It's typical to use "human" as the subject "[the subject is large]."
Really means "I don't want to do that job, I want the computer to do it."
It is [overgeneralization] to extend it to different people because each of these "selves" has a different weighting of time, motivation, and money.

There are many people who would like to have AI do a job if they can pay 10 yen as the call cost of AI, but when the cost becomes 100 yen, 1,000 yen, or 10,000 yen, many people give up the option of having AI do the job.
In that case, sometimes it's "I'll do it myself" and sometimes it's "I won't do it."
Those who "don't do it" aren't originally so eager to make it happen.

> I believe there is only one reason for Japan's decline, and that is because "entrepreneurs are stuck in Japan, complaining about a country they don't even know.
> Japanese businessmen are stationed in all kinds of countries to earn foreign currency by sticking around and supporting the local economy.
> Japan's current entrepreneurs are just subcontractors to them. So the market capitalization ranking in Japan will not be replaced. It is natural.
> In addition, Chinese, Indians, Jews, and other players in the developing economies are fluttering to all countries to conduct business.

>[nishio https://x.com/nishio/status/1966494483614462017] When an elder who thinks he is superior says something negative about a young person who finds something interesting, it is usually because he is afraid that the young person who is supposed to be inferior to him will be the one to say, "I am superior and I have found something interesting. lines.text: People who are proud of what they don't have.
Throw it away."
[Zen (Buddhism)]
[GPT5.icon]
Throw it away" is a famous Zen phrase "[authored by a free hand] (hogejaku)." A typical episode is the following [koan].
Itum-yang-sonja asks Zhaoju: "What should I do if I have nothing in my life?
ZHAO ZHOU: "Let go and write (throw away)."
The Venerable One: "What do you throw away when you have nothing more?"
Zhaozhou: "If you can't throw it away, carry it with you" - there the Venerable One realized. ([ddc.shengyen.org https://ddc.shengyen.org/?doc=04-12-037&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
What to "throw away"?
We discard the "grasping mind" instead of the object.

The key is the fall that we must let go of even the notion of "having nothing." It removes the attachment to the throw away/not throw away dichotomy in one stroke. ([ddc.shengyen.org https://ddc.shengyen.org/?doc=04-12-037&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Practical implications

Dogen defines the essentials of zazen as "letting go of all worldly desires, resting and doing all things, and not thinking about good and evil. In other words, the idea is to put aside the evaluation of good and evil, and to simply sit and learn through experience to "detach oneself from body and mind. ([Scribd https://www.scribd.com/doc/84868885/%E9%81%93%E5%85%83%E7%A6%AA%E5%B8%AB%E7%9A%84%E5%9D%90%E7%A6%AA%E8%A7%80?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Sister Arc of the "Throw Away" Motif (Ref.)

Tanxia Yakibutsu: An anecdote about a wooden Buddha image that was burned to keep it warm. It is told as a poignant metaphor for burning away attachment to idols (forms) and returning to the essence. ([engakuji.or.jp https://www.engakuji.or.jp/blog/37324/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Monk carrying a woman on his back by the river: An older monk carries a woman on his back, and when the younger monk later blames him, he responds, "I have already taken her down. When the young monk later blames the elder monk for carrying the woman, the elder monk responds, "I have already let her down, and you are still carrying her on your back. The story is about a young monk who is blamed by an older monk for carrying a woman and later responds, "I have already carried the woman on my back. ([The Still State https://thestillstatemeditation.com/how-to-let-go-of-the-past-a-story-of-mindfulness-and-freedom/?utm_source= chatgpt.com])
Tips on how to use (very practical)
1. name the evaluation, anxiety, and conclusion you are grasping now in your mind in one word (e.g., "anxiety").
2. chant in your mind, "Houkaishaku," and then relax with a "huff" in time with your exhalation.
3. if it still does not leave, just be aware that you are "carrying it" (because resistance = reattachment).
-- This "awareness, loosening, and awareness of adherence" is itself a daily repetition of the three lines of the koan.

différance
[GPT5.icon]
Derrida's "différance, [différance]" means

The meaning is coined by Derrida to refer to the function of a "difference" that rises up and is never fixed in its final form, but is always "delayed" to another sign. The French word différance, which is the same sound as différence, embodies a critique of phonocentrism in that it is indistinguishable in pronunciation, and only the scribe can distinguish it.
Core Idea (in formula)
Difference = difference + deferral + espacement
[difference]: following Saussure, the meaning of a word can only come from its difference from another word.
→ [value based on difference]
[delay]: meaning is postponed to the next word in the lexical chain, and the final definite point (transcendental symbolic content) is not reached.
[Spacing]: The **intervals (spaces)** between segments create structure and shift meaning in time and space.
[trace] (trace): no meaning leaves traces of other symbols, and there is no complete "[present]".
Aim (point of criticism)
The **"metaphysics of the present "** of Western metaphysics (the idea of privileging origin, center, and pure meaning) and the dismantling of logocentrism/phonocentrism.
It shakes up the myth of the origin of meaning, subject and text, and encourages reading practices (deconstruction).
Mini Example
The meaning of "cat" is established by the difference between "not a dog, mammal, pet..." and other words, and the explanation continues to extend to other words.
différance and différence are the same in voice. Only the letters show the difference - this reversal is Derrida's point.
Common Misconceptions
Not an exemption from relativism: a principle to read strictly in line with the web of differences and delays, not to say that everything is OK.
Not a fixed "concept": rather a "quasi-concept/operation". A position that is doubtful of being tightly defined and closed itself.
related term
Ecriture (scribe)/supplement/arche-writing/dissemination, etc.
reference text
Differences" (speech delivered in 1968, later published in Philosophical Margins)
On Grammatology" (1967)
Voices and Phenomena" (1967)

Summary of "value based on difference (valeur)" in [Saussure

The idea that the "value" of a [linguistic unit] (word, phoneme, etc.) arises from the [web of relations] of how that unit differs from and is connected to other units. Each element is not determined by its unique substantive meaning, but is positioned by its differences within the system.
Mechanism (relationship between the two)
Syntagmatic: a relation that actually lines up. Constraints and roles created by the conjunction of words such as "black + cat + meows".
Association/paradigmatic relationship: a selection relationship of candidates that can be replaced in the same position. Substitutability, such as "black/white/big...cat".
➡︎ The value of a word,
(1) what it can be coupled with (connectivity/function), and (2) what it can be coupled with (connectivity/function),
(2) What is it distinguished from in normative terms (conflict and substitutability)?
This is determined as the overall result of the
[nishio.icon]I feel this is related to [word2vec], which says that the meaning of a word can be calculated based on the distribution of surrounding words.
key point

1. product of difference: language is said to be "composed only of differences and has no positive terms". The opposition between /p/ and /b/ (voiced, voiceless, etc.) is given more value than the nature of the sound itself.

2. arbitrariness and convention: the connection between nōgi (sound forms) and shōgi (ideas) is not a natural necessity, but depends on social conventions. Hence, values are intra-system relative and vary from language to language.

Example of language differences: French mouton can refer to both "sheep" and "mutton," while English is divided into sheep and mutton. Rather than a difference in the "meaning" of words, a difference in the way the system is cut (i.e., the way differences are established) creates a difference in value.
[nishio.icon]This is [segmentation].

4. chess/currency metaphor: The value of a chess piece is not determined by its material, but by its relationship to other pieces and rules. Currency also has value not because of the inherent properties of the metal, but because of the exchange relationship within the system. Similarly for words, position (relationship) = value.
Difference (practically) between "value" and "meaning."
Meaning (SIGNIFICATION): a description of what a word refers to.
Value (valeur): the position the word occupies in the system (what it can be connected with, what it cannot replace, what it is opposed to).
Even if they refer to the same object, different systems have different values (sheep/mutton example above).
Points that are often misunderstood
Value is not "frequency of use or social reputation". Technical terms based on relationships within the structure.
Value is not a fixed entity. They change in tandem when the overall arrangement of vocabulary and phonology changes.

A comprehensive review that organizes a system of techniques to compensate for the weaknesses of RAG (ignoring relationships, redundant context, lack of the big picture) by utilizing graph structure (KG/TAG) to achieve more accurate and contextual understanding of the generation.
What's new.
GraphRAG formulation:
1.[G-Indexing] (graph construction and indexing)
2.[G-Retrieval] (Retrieval of node/triple/path/subgraph)
3.[G-Generation] (Generate acquisition graph as input)
Utilizes relational knowledge and global structures that are difficult to pick up in string RAGs, and is advantageous in QFS, etc.
G-Indexing (graph infrastructure)
Data source: open KG (Wikidata/ConceptNet, etc.) / own construction (TAG from documents, tables, logs).
Index:
Graph Indexing (Structure Search)
Text index (Template conversion → BM25/dense search)
Vector index (node/egonet embedding)
Hybrid recommended.
G-Retrieval
Retrievers: non-parametric (BFS/shortest path/PCST), LM systems, GNN systems, or combined.
Paradigm: batch/repeat (adaptive/non-adaptive)/multi-stage (coarse to fine).
Granularity: node, triple, path, subgraph, mixed.
Enhancement: query expansion/decomposition, knowledge merge/pruning (re-ranking, PageRank, LLM checks, etc.)
G-Generation
Generator:
GNN (strong in discrimination tasks)
LM (strong in generation/reasoning)
Hybrid: cascade (GNN to LM prefix)/parallel (representation coupling and output integration).
LM input format for graphs:
Graph language (edge tables, natural sentences, code-like notation, syntax trees, node sequences)
Graph embedding (fused by Prefix/Prompt Tuning or FiD).
Generation enhancement: pre (rewriting and planning) / during (constraint decoding, etc.) / post (answer integration and verification).
learning
No learning required: rule search + prompts, embedded similarity.
With learning: Supervision/remote supervision/RL/self-supervision to optimize the retriever/generator.
Collaborative learning: mutual reinforcement for alternate learning and integration purposes.
Application and evaluation
Tasks: KBQA/CSQA, EL/RE, fact verification, link prediction, dialogue, recommendation.
Areas: e-commerce, medical, academic, legal, literary, etc.
Bench: WebQSP/CWQ/HotpotQA, etc., STaRK, GraphQA, GRBENCH, CRAG.
Indicators: EM/F1/Accuracy/BLEU types + acquisition quality (coverage, diversity, fidelity).
Industry Case Studies
Microsoft GraphRAG (QFS enhanced with community summary), NebulaGraph Edition, Ant Group Edition, Neo4j NaLLM/Graph Builder, etc.
Future Issues
Dynamic graph updating and adaptation, multimodal integration, and efficiency in large graphs,
Linkage with Graph Foundation Models, lossless compression to mitigate long-text problems, standard bench maintenance, and application extensions.
Practical tips (super summary)
Hybrid indexing + multi-stage acquisition for accuracy/cost optimization even on a small scale.
Select granularity (path/subgraph center) according to the task.
LM input should be in short, complete, readable graph language (community summary if necessary).
Critical phases are stabilized when re-ranking/pruning and post-verification are included.

[tagging] of [bottom-up]
[KJ method]
[Cumulative effect of ideas]
[Information Organization 3.0]
[GPT5.icon]
"Bottom-up tagging" super-summary (3 lines)
Instead of a pre-designed classification tree, a knowledge network is developed by adding links (=tags) that spontaneously arise from the memos.
This is a practice that transplants the KJ method's "nameplate creation/convergence" to digital and turns the cumulative effect of ideas (underdevelopment → stability → inclusion → downfall).
Scrapbox/Cosense emphasizes "divergence = branching/convergence = links across branches" in a lincographic manner, with page links and row links at the core.
[nishio.icon]I think it's amazing that you were able to generate this with only 4 lines of input.
It's all missing from the generated product because there was no mention of the crucial Information Organization 3.0 in the range that can be traced by the link.
I asked GPT5Think and got an easy answer.
Core Principles (excerpts)
Top-down classification is minimal: assumption that structure changes with additional knowledge. Fixed trees lead to "dead text". Store in a network.
Linking is the tag: [[page link]] rather than #hash, and use line links to establish a concrete relationship. Do not break references just by copying them.
Visualize moments of convergence: lines connecting different groups = convergent thinking (critical backlink). This is the point of progress of knowledge.
Life cycle of ideas:
Undeveloped (hypothetical sprout) → Stable (reappearance of isomorphism) → Inclusive (combines with other elements and becomes higher order)/Falls (dismissed due to contradiction). Record and turn.
Operational flow (divergence → convergence in the shortest distance)
1. divergence (10 minutes)
Drop a small specific memo (1 memo = 1 claim/1 fact).
If in doubt, don't force tagging = put it underdeveloped.
2. light convergence (10 minutes)
Add at least two links to each memo (e.g., related concepts/ counterexamples).
Use line links to clarify "which line and which line resonated" (aiming for critical backlinks).
3. making a nameplate (10 minutes)
Attach headings and one-sentence summaries to adjacent pages (the "faceplates" of the KJ method).
Assign a "state tag" on the spot: 🍼Undeveloped/🧱Stable/🕸Inclusive/🗑Fallen.
Point: Write first, then connect later, then summarize, in this order, and then write a clean copy (one-dimensional book) at the end.
Linking & Tagging Conventions (Mini-Conventions)
Noun for page name (short and unambiguous)/synonym puts a thin page for redirects.
Line link first: Copying and pasting quotations is convenient, but breaks references. Link to the original line whenever possible.
A minimum set of related terms (optional): `is-a / part-of / supports / refutes / example-of` may be written at the beginning of each line (over-labeling is x).
Measure and review (lightweight KPIs)
Isolation rate: Isolated pages divided by total pages (the lower the better).
Average number of backlinks: a measure of convergence (the higher the better).
Critical ratio: percentage of rows with multiple backlinks (the "bud" of convergence).
Number of inclusive events: Number of newly established links between different clusters.
In both cases, it is sufficient to use Scrapbox's list of links for manual measurement → count only monthly.
anti-pattern
Make a huge category table ahead of time/struggle with classification as you write.
Reference cutoff by copying and pasting (erasing evidence of convergence).
Premature clearing (tree fixing) kills the network.
A move right now (in 15 minutes)
Select 5 items from today's notes and add 2 links + status tag to each.
Add a nameplate line (title + one sentence) to the connected islets.
Make sure to create "one across the branch" (i.e., one seed of convergence).
If necessary, this operation can be canvassed into a one-page "Operating Rules" (with sample templates).

In [Scrapbox Information Organization], [Tadanori Kurashita] divided the history of information organization into three categories
Information Organization 1.0: Location-based Organization
Things can only exist in one place at a time.
The same idea applies to placing files in a hierarchy of folders.
If something can't be clearly defined where it's located, it's out of order.
Information Organization 2.0: Don't Organize, Arrange
Arrange them in order of update or access, rather than trying to organize them.
Find by search
Search = Refine
Google has been successful in aligning by PageRank
Services without a good ranking method tend to be "sorted by update time", etc.
Sorting by access order is a rule of thumb that "things that have been used recently are used more often again".
[Information Organization 3.0] :
Networked organization, connected by links

When certain information is used, the information that [relevance] to it is used more often.

The "box metaphor" and "tag metaphor" of "assignment."
[nishio.icon] Explanation of "[Box Metaphor]" in "[Assignment]" and its inconvenience and "[Tag Metaphor]".
[GPT5.icon]
Two metaphors for "assignment
[** 1) Box metaphor].
Variables = "boxes" for contents
Assignment = copying a value into a box
Open the box and read the contents (value) each time you refer to it.
Situations that can be explained well
A sense in which a primitive value is placed on the stack, such as `int x=3;` in C
Explanation of value semantics (copy) assumptions
Inconvenient and misleading points
1. overlooking sharing (aliasing)
It is easy to misunderstand "copy the whole box" in a language that shares objects and arrays.
code:python
a = [1,2]; b = a # Reference to the same list in b
b.append(3)
# In the box metaphor, it's supposed to be "another box" but in fact a changes too -> confusion
2. misunderstanding of argument passing
Invites the "pass-by-value vs. pass-by-reference" debate: Python/JS is "pass by-reference to an object" = touches the same object as the caller, but a box can easily look like "pass-by-copy".
3. confusion between reassignment and modification
Reassignment: variable changes to point to a different object
Change: Change the internal state of the same object
With a box, it is easy to mix up the two.
2) Tag/Label metaphor
The object (value entity) exists first, and the variable is a "tag" that is attached to the object.
Assignment = Change to which object a certain tag name is pasted (bound).
Multiple tags can be placed on the same subject (alias = alias)
Change is "change of subject" and reassignment is "re-pasting of tags"
advantage
Alias references and identifications can be explained naturally
code:python
y = x # I put a new tag y on the same object
y.append(3) # The object itself is modified, so it changes from x's point of view
x is y # True (same object)
The identity of the reassignment is clear.
code:python
y = [9] # Replace the tag of y with another target. The original target is retained by x
Clear distinction between immutable and mutable.
Immutable (number, string, tuple, etc.): The content of the object does not change. Change is always "create a new object and replace the tag."
Mutable (arrays, dictionaries, etc.): can change the target on the fly
GC's intuition: if no tag is attached to any object, it is subject to collection.
Which language is best suited for
Compatibility with Python / JavaScript / Ruby / Java (reference types) and other reference semantics-centric explanations
Box intuition still useful for C primitives (used together as needed)
Sorting out common confusions (rephrased in tags)
function argument
A new temporary argument tag pasted on the target exists only during the call.
If the target is changed, the caller is also reflected. Even if a temporary argument is replaced with a different target, the caller's tag remains unchanged.
code:python
def f(v):
v.append(0) # change target -> reflect in share
v = [9] # v's tag re-paste -> irrelevant for the calling tag
Shallow copy / deep copy

In the tag metaphor, shallow copying is "only the outer object is new, while the inner object is reused tags to the same object as the original". Deep copying is "creating and pasting a new object on the inside as well.
code:python
import copy
b = copy.copy(a) # shallow
c = copy.deepcopy(a)
Distinguish between reassignment and mutation (very important)
code:javascript
let a = {n:1};
let b = a; // b tag on the same object
a = {n:2}; // a tag is pasted to another object (b is not affected)
b.n = 3; // change the "original object" that b points to (independent of a)
Guideline for use (abbreviated version)
Box meta: useful for explaining primitives with value copying assumptions and basic types in C
Tag Meta: appropriate for explaining objects/references, variability, aliases, GC in modern languages (less misunderstanding)
one-line summary
Box = "value in a variable"
Tag = "Variable is "to which subject is the name tag attached."
If the reference, variable, and argument behavior is correctly intuited, the tag metaphor is safe.

Philosophy of Eugene Gendlin
[GPT5.icon]

[Eugene Gendlin.] ([Eugene Gendlin], 1926-2017) was a philosopher and psychologist, best known as an advocate of "[focusing]." His philosophy has a unique system of thought that focuses on the relationship between experience and meaning. It is organized and explained below.
1.  [process of experience] （[Experiencing]）
At the core of the Gendlin philosophy is the concept of "experience process.
Human experience exists as [a flow of ambiguous wholeness before it is verbalized], not as mere sensations or feelings.
This is also called "[felt sense], [felt sense], [Felt Meaning]," and refers to an ambiguous sensation that cannot yet be put into words, but is certainly felt in the body.
→ For him, philosophy and psychotherapy are activities that access this "[preverbal] experience" and create new expressions and understandings from it.
2. interaction between language and experience
Gendlin believed that "[language] must be rooted in experience.
[Words have meaning when they come into contact with experiences], and experiences are organized and expanded by words.
This [reciprocation generates new insights].
There is uniqueness here in its emphasis on [corporeality] and [generativity], as opposed to a mere analytic-philosophical view of language.
3. "[Implicit order]" ([Implicit order])
The human experience always includes the possibility of "[how it] will unfold next.
When an unspoken, ambiguous feeling (implicit) encounters an appropriate word or expression, it becomes clear, "Yes, that's it," and develops into a new understanding.
[nishio.icon][Encountering the right words helps you move toward [a new understanding].
This process is supposed to be a source of philosophical contemplation and [creativity] as well as psychotherapeutic change.
4. focusing and philosophy
Gendlin is also a practitioner of [psychotherapy] and has systematized the methodology that emerged from his experience as "Focusing.
A method of deepening [new awareness] and [self-understanding] by bringing the client's attention to the process of his or her own experience.
Philosophically, the experience itself is "[the] material of thought" and is emphasized as a fundamental dimension that precedes theorizing.
5. impact and positioning
Gendlin's characteristic is that he continued in the vein of [hussar] and [Merleau-Ponty.]'s [phenomenology], but connected it to the practice of psychotherapy.
The position that "thought is rooted in experience" is closer to [pragmatism] and [existentialism] than to the formal logic of analytic philosophy.
In his later philosophy, he developed a [dynamic understanding of existence] that could be understood as "[process philosophy].
summary
Gendlin's philosophy can be organized as follows:
1. emphasis on "experiential process" before language
2. new meanings are generated through the interaction of language and experience
3. "Implicit order" directs the following understanding
4. practical ideas bridging philosophy and psychotherapy

pages.title: How to deal with self-justification loops

lines.text: How to deal with self-justification loops
[GPT5.icon]
Signs of a self-justifying loop
Habit of replacing evaluation indicators after failure ([goal post moving]).
Phrases without [falsifiability] (e.g., "It's really working, but I don't see it yet").
How to deal with self-justification loops
Pre-fixed: The evaluation period, scope, and indicators (KPIs) are determined ahead of time and not moved until later.
Rejection condition: pre-determined numerical disqualification line (e.g., if the error >25 pts in 4 weeks, it is discontinued).
Calibration by prediction: Produce a prediction with probability for each interpretation and periodically grade the accuracy with [Brier], etc.
[reverse question] check: "If this interpretation is wrong, what are the first signs that it appears?" as a monitoring indicator.
Preserving alternatives: mainstay interpretation + alternative hypotheses for comparison run side by side and rebased quarterly.

Usefulness to one's life
[nishio.icon]Who has historically advocated the position that pragmatism is true or false according to [usefulness] for [My Life]?
[GPT5.icon]

The most direct statement of "usefulness = truth" was made by [William James] in his 1907 Pragmatism Lecture VI: "The 'true thing' is, in short, what is [[useful] (expedient) in the way our thoughts proceed," and he explained truth in terms of the practical utility of this He explained the truth in terms of the practical utility of "[cash-value]" ([Brock University ]). ([Brock University https://brocku.ca/MeadProject/James/James_1907/James_1907_06.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[nishio.icon] You mention cash-value, but "useful in the way we think" reminds me of [thought economy theory].

[F.C.S. Schiller] (English pragmatist/humanist) developed the same point with the formulation "What works (works) is true". James himself introduced it as such in Lecture VI, and Schiller's main book, [Studies in Humanism] (1907), develops the same line of argument. ([Brock University https://brocku.ca/MeadProject/James/James_1907/James_1907_06.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
(With only historical facts for contrast)

[C.S. Parse] ([parse]) linked truth to "[the opinion reached by the community at the ultimate of inquiry]" and distinguished it from the short-term utility of the individual. ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, https://plato.stanford.edu/archives/sum2025/entries/truth-pragmatic/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[John Dewey] instrumentally rephrased the "truth" concept as "[warranted assertibility]" ([Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/dewey/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
In short, James (along with Schiller) is the historical representative who spoke truth with a strong emphasis on "usefulness to one's life" in the foreground.
[nishio.icon]James, Perth and Dewey seem to be saying totally different things, how are they related?
[GPT5.icon]The "connection" and "division of roles" among the three parties
Common Core (Pragmatic Maxim)
The idea that "the meaning of a concept is exhausted by the practical consequences of that concept."
It was formulated by Perls in the late 19th century, popularized by James for the general public, and developed by Dewey as a methodology for scientific inquiry and social practice.
Division of roles (where to place emphasis)
Perth: Semantic Criteria and the Logic of Inquiry

Truth = "[an opinion to which the community converges at the extreme end of endless inquiry]". Emphasis on long-term, [public] consensus, not individual convenience. Later renamed "[pragmaticism]" to distance it from Jamesianism.
[careful deliberation] や[社会的意思決定]との関連がありそう[nishio.icon]
James: [the pragmatic theory of truth] (CASH VALUE)

Truth = "the actual usefulness (successfully guiding an action) before experience". Characterized by speaking from a ground close to the concrete life and preferences of the individual. Popularizes the idea of parsing, but presents the theory of truth in a more plastic way.
Dewey: instrumentalism/methods of inquiry

Rephrasing the word truth as substantially "guaranteed assertability. Embedding pragmatism in the process of [collective problem solving] as experimentalism linking schooling, democracy, and technology.
How it is "related" (key points)
1. the starting point is the perspective ([meaning = practical result]).
2. popularized by James (extending the semantic criterion to truth theory and emphasizing [individual usefulness]).
3. institutionalized by Dewey (reconfigured as a procedure of scientific, educational, and democratic inquiry, with emphasis on [public problem solving] rather than individuals).
Similarities and differences (shortest comparison)
table:_
Perspectives Perth James Dewey
Main focus Semantic criteria of concepts, logic of inquiry Pragmatic theory of truth Methods of inquiry, social implementation
Truth Long-term convergence of community Working and useful (context-dependent, individual-leaning) Guaranteed assertability (procedure-dependent, public-leaning)
Tone Anti-Psychologism, Realism-leaning Pluralism, Empiricism Experimentalism, Instrumentalism
In short, while the three parties share **the same core (outcome-based meaning making)**,
Perspective is meaning and long-term exploration,
James is a truth in line with personal experience,
Dewey is a public problem-solving process
The relationship between the two is that they were developed by shifting the focus of each to the other.
