Markets, Hierarchies, and Communities
[GPT5.icon]
The market (as a concept), the level, and the community" = the three basic principles of "how to coordinate work" in society. Just to the point.
1) Price / Market
How it works: Decentralized decision making with price signals. Transactions are made on a contract basis.
Strengths: Fast resource allocation / Induces ingenuity / Easy exit and entry.
Weaknesses: underprovision of externalities (environment and safety) and public goods / asymmetric information.
Examples: B2B ordering, cloud pay-as-you-go, ad bidding.
Suitable conditions: results can be clearly measured, standardized, and competitive.
Indicators to look at: price elasticity, margin, bid/contract ratio.
2) Hierarchy / Firm & Bureaucracy
Mechanism: Coordinated by orders and plans within the organization. Long-term investment and bundling of resources.
Strengths: Large-scale coordination, quality control, and clear responsibilities.
Weaknesses: bureaucratization, information lag, stagnation of innovation.
Examples: supply chain management for a company, business operations for a government agency.
Suitable conditions: high interdependence, confidentiality, long-term and large-scale projects.
Indicators to watch: lead time, quality defect rate, organizational MTTR, fixed cost ratio.
3) Communities (Communities / Norms & Commons)
Mechanism: Coordinated by shared norms, reputation, and voluntary contributions. Results go to the commons.
Strengths: Fast accumulation and reuse of knowledge, low participation costs.
Weaknesses: dependence on gratis, governance burden, and weak circulation of funds.
Examples: OSS, Wikipedia, industry standards bodies, regional cooperation.
Suitable conditions: results are non-competitive (knowledge) and have high reuse value.
Indicators to watch: number of maintainers, Issue retention, number of forks, maintenance fund inflows.
Usage and hybrids
Market x hierarchy: companies plan internally while externally procure at a price (typical supply network).
Market x Community: commercial SaaS based on OSS (market for price, commons for infrastructure).
Hierarchy x Community: Companies agree on specifications with standardization bodies → internal implementation.
Contemporary Supplement
Platform and AI recommendations affect the market/community as a "quasi-plan" (exposure and search = substantial adjustments).
The state is the fourth pole that supports the three parties through internalization of externalities, safety standards, and public procurement.
super-summary
Market = "price" for dispersion adjustment
Hierarchy = "order and plan" for centralized coordination
Autonomous adjustment based on community = "norms and reputation
In practice, it is best to design a combination of all three.
[work coordination].
[Adjustment mechanism]
I asked where this triangle came from (source).[nishio.icon]
[GPT5.icon]

There is. However, the "triangle" was not presented as it was by a single classic, but was reconstituted by superimposing the community/commons as a third coordinating principle on the classic that formulated the market ↔ hierarchy (corporations).
Market vs. hierarchy classics

Coase, "The Nature of the Firm" (1937): Why transactions are conducted "within the firm (hierarchy)" rather than in the marketplace = explained in [Transaction costs]. ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1468-0335.1937.tb00002.x?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Williamson, Markets and Hierarchies (1975): develops transaction cost theory and analyzes the boundaries and choices between markets and hierarchies. ([SSRN https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=1496220&utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Presentation of the third principle (community/network)

Powell, "Neither Markets nor Hierarchies: Network Organizations" (1990): theorizes "networks" (= communal coordination) as a third form. ([Stanford University https://web.stanford.edu/~woodyp/powell_neither.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Ostrom, Governing the Commons (1990): a demonstration of autonomous governance of the commons independent of the state or private ownership. A Strong Foundation for Community Principles. ([Cambridge University Press & Assessment https://www.cambridge.org/core/books/governing-the-commons/reflections-on-the-commons/25EA7 EDBB48EEC9BA6A761E978EA9BA1?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
[Elinor Ostrom]

Adler & Heckscher (2006), The Firm as a Collaborative Community: systematizing collaborative communities in the knowledge economy as organizational forms. ([smlr.rutgers.edu https://smlr.rutgers.edu/sites/smlr/files/Documents/Faculty-Staff-Docs/The%20Firm%20as%20a%20Collaborative%20 Community%20%28Heckscher-Adler%29-%20Contents%20and%20Introduction%20%281%29.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

In short, it is positioned as a widely referenced "market-hierarchy-community" triangle used in practice, based on Coase/Williamson's "market x hierarchy" axis plus the community/network of Powell, Ostrom, and Adler.

double-empathy problem
[GPT5.icon]
What is the Double Empathy Problem?
The concept refers to "mutual" comprehension difficulties that occur between individuals on the [autistic spectrum] ([ASD]) and non-ASD individuals.

The ASD side is not "flawed," but rather, it is seen as a misreading of the other's intentions and feelings by both parties due to misalignment of different experiences, norms, and communication styles (as proposed by Damian Milton, 2012).
main point
Bidirectional: Misunderstandings are not a one-sided problem. It is easy for both sides to misunderstand the assumptions and context of the other.
Context-dependent: Interpretation habits that are optimized for "neurotypicals similar to oneself" with whom one normally interacts are less likely to apply to others who are different.
Structural factors: When places and rules are designed according to the social majority (non-ASD) standard, only the ASD side tends to be asked to be considered = fixed misunderstanding.
typical example

Inclusion and implicit cues (eye contact, sarcasm) in chit-chat are operated under the majority assumption → ASD side has difficulty in taking in the meaning. On the other hand, frank and specific expressions on the ASD side are misunderstood as "[blunt]" by the non-ASD side.
Email: ASD's brief and direct writing of requirements is received as "Are you angry?" and the ASD side feels the vague euphemism is unintended.
Points that are often misunderstood
×x "ASD is not empathetic."
→ Just different methods; ASDs are more empathetic to details and concrete experiences and often understand more deeply with explicit information and time than with implicit reading.
×x "The ASD side can be fixed by training."
→ Need to design the place and learn both sides (bi-directional adaptation).
Solution Tips (Practical)
Explicit: Verbalize objectives, agreements, and next actions. Do not rely on tacit "airs and graces.
Meta-conversation: Discussing the "rules" of communication itself (e.g., reply speed, format, meaning of pictograms, etc.).
Media design: minutes, bullet points, summary columns, and term definitions. Text assistance for synchronous conversations.
Co-reading/co-experiencing: Examine the same material (text, case study) together slowly and match the correspondence between feelings and words.

Diversification of evaluations: Avoid evaluation of "social skills" based on a single indicator such as eye contact or chatting skills, and include evaluation of achievements and considerate behavior.
In a nutshell:

The other party and I are 'different operating systems. If we can share the same protocol (rules) without assuming that we can understand each other without an interpreter, misunderstandings will decrease.

[ASD is not a lack of empathy.]

Add "nation" and "model" to the triangle.
prev: [market, hierarchy, community].
[GPT5.icon]
Copy. Based on the premise of the triangle (market, hierarchy, and community), the pentagonal model as an "extended" version of the triangle will be explained in a compact manner.
What is the Pentagonal Model?

A framework designed on the premise that five "forces" are simultaneously deployed and interfere with each other by adding **State (State) and Model (AI, Algorithm, Platform)** to the three coordination principles.
Market: Diversification adjustment with price signals
Hierarchy: Centralized coordination with orders and plans
Community: autonomous adjustment by norms and reputation
State: coordination with enforcement in laws, regulations, supervision, and public procurement
Model: Implement "invisible planning" with recommendations, search rankings, dynamic pricing, etc.
Why we need two additional poles (one per line)
State: Standards, certifications, subsidies, and sanctions were the main causes of the simultaneous rearrangement of supply networks.
Model: platform algo permanently reallocates demand, exposure, and labor allocation (quasi-planned economy).
(omitted)
Rearrangement of positioning (triangle -> pentagon)
The triangle is still the core. However, states and models are treated as operable levers, not "exogenous environments.
Result: Clear delineation of responsibility and avoiding misinterpretation of policy/algo changes as "market whims".
Outcome: adaptability during normal times + resilience during disturbances can be maximized at the same time.
super-summary
Add the state and model to the triangle and design and monitor five adjustment levers simultaneously.
Measures will be evaluated on three layers of information x logistics x energy, switching between the two phases of peacetime/disturbance.
This allows on-demand diversity peer production to operate as a complementary cycle.
**The "necessity "** of adding "state" and "model" to the triangle is explained in detail, not in a single line (avoiding implementation theory and concentrating on concepts and phenomena).
1) Why make "State" an independent pole?
(a) Qualitatively different adjustment mechanisms
The state redefines the space of action itself with coercive power (law, licensing, sanctions, taxation, subsidies), whereas market = price, hierarchy = command, community = norm.
The state can change the **boundary conditions (what is allowed/required)** that prices and internal orders are "given" from a higher level.
(b) The range and simultaneity of effects are orders of magnitude greater

Simultaneity: Carbon taxes, medical and construction certifications, import/export regulations, infrastructure fees, etc. will be applied simultaneously to all players, rearranging the supply chain all at once.
Cross-border: tariffs, embargoes, and data cross-border regulations move borders that companies and communities cannot move.
(c) In triangles, the explanation escapes to "exogenous shocks".

For example, even if the market structure shifts in the case of public procurement (a huge demand of the state), the triangular shape of the market would be simply "the market has changed," and the state as an "operable lever" would not be visible.
As a result, policy-induced changes are misinterpreted as price changes, resulting in erroneous learning and optimization.
(d) Response to counterexample.
Response: "State intervention can be internalized in prices (fines = costs)."
→ Fines are only partially applied. The core is **"non-priceable" restrictions** such as entry bans, business suspensions, confiscation, criminal penalties, etc.
Response: "Regulation is a corporate lobby, a de facto market."
→ The existence of lobbying activities is not denied, but only the state has the power to enforce final decisions.
2) Why make "Model (Model: AI, Algorithm, Platform)" an independent pole?
(a) The medium of adjustment is "neither price nor command nor norm."
Algorithmic interventions such as exposure, recommendations, search rankings, matching, rate limiting, dynamic pricing, etc., permanently redistribute demand, labor, and information flows.
This functions as a quasi-plan because it precedes and runs parallel to prices (the market) and forms the front end of the decision-making process.
(b) Minor design changes spill over into huge real economy

One coefficient of recommendation, one throttle threshold of API, and sales, visibility, participation rates, and travel demand are transferred on a large scale ("gatekeeping" nature of the platform economy).
Moreover, changes are high frequency and private, which differs from the transparent decision-making process of hierarchy and community.
(c) Reasons why inclusions into triangles fail.
If we reduce it to "part of the market (ad prices)" or "part of the company's internal orders (product decisions)," we cannot see which "algo intervention" is the main body of causation.
Exposure/recommendation is often a zero sum allocation problem (if you raise someone, someone else will go down). Prices and norms alone cannot describe it.
(d) Response to counterexample.
Counterargument: "Algos can operate under community norms (OSS-ization)."
→ Possible, but most of them are black boxes of private companies. And even with OSS, if data and distribution rules are managed separately, they remain as independent poles.
Response: "The model is a tool of corporate "hierarchy
→ A social lever that goes beyond the usual hierarchical imperative in that it continuously reallocates the action space of external players, even if the decision is made within a company.
3) Advantages (theoretical and practical) of considering the two as "independent poles
(Theory) Increased explanatory power
We can separate and model the causality of policy shock-driven rearrangements (tariffs, certifications, subsidies) and algo-driven rearrangements (exposure, search, fees).
Phenomena that tend to be pushed out as "exogenous variables" in triangles can be treated as endogenous levers.
(Practice) Liability Boundary and Observability
The "whose levers moved what" can be tracked in the **Change History (Official Gazette and Release Notes)**.
Reproducible verification of policy and algo changes without confusing them with "market whims" (A/B Impact Assessment).
(Risk) Address heterogeneity of failure modes
State: excess, delay, arbitrariness / Model: opacity, bias, runaway - risks of a different system than market, hierarchy, community.
By separating the poles, the audit and remediation design can be tailored to each.
4) How far is a "state/model" and how far is a triangle (boundary conditions)?
When the state pole is weakened: In less effective laws (failed states), markets, hierarchies, and communities are relatively led.
If the model pole is thin: If fully transparent recommendations, public APIs, collaborative governance, and data commons are established, the model pole can be absorbed by the community pole.
Criteria for practical decisions:
1. enforceability (non-price penalty for non-compliance)
2. control of front-end allocation (who decides what is "visible/encounterable/usable")
3. simultaneity, frequency, and transparency of changes
summary
The state is the higher mechanism that forcibly rewrites the "premise" of prices and orders,
The model is a quasi-planning mechanism that constantly reallocates the "front end" of decision-making,

Therefore, it is reasonable to set up the two as independent poles, rather than encompassing them in a triangle, in terms of explanatory power of the phenomenon, delimitation of responsibility, and risk design.

**The idea of treating the state and the model (algorithm/platform)** as independent poles, based on the triangle (market, hierarchy, community), is a "junction" of the classics below and recent "platform/algorithm governance" research.
Triangular base

Formulation of market x hierarchy boundaries: Coase (1937)/Williamson (1975). Explained by the use of "orders and plans" and market transactions within firms = transaction costs. ([rochelleterman.com https://rochelleterman.com/ir/sites/default/files/Coase%201937.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Third form (network/community): Powell (1990) presents a network organization that is "neither market nor hierarchical"; Ostrom (1990) demonstrates autonomous governance of the commons; Powell (1990) presents a network organization that is "neither market nor hierarchical"; Ostrom (1990) demonstrates autonomous governance of the commons. ([Stanford University https://web.stanford.edu/~woodyp/powell_neither.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Basis for considering the "State" as an independent pole.

A "higher-level mechanism" that simultaneously reconfigures the assumptions of the behavioral space through legal enforcement, such as regulations, certifications, tariffs, and public procurement. See also Williamson's review and retrospect. ([Stanford Graduate School of Business, https://www.gsb.stanford.edu/faculty-research/books/firms-markets-hierarchies-transaction-cost-economics- perspective?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
Basis for considering "model (algo/PF)" as an independent pole

[Code is Law: [Lessig] argues that architecture (code) is the "fourth regulation" that regulates behavior. A regulating medium different from prices, commands, and norms. ([harvardmagazine.com https://www.harvardmagazine.com/2000/01/code-is-law-html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[Algorithmic governance]/regulation: [Yeung (2018)] theorizes "[algorithmic regulation]" in which recommendation, scoring, dynamic pricing, etc., continuously modify behavior. ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/rego.12158?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

[platform governance]: Gillespie (2018) describes "gatekeeping" where moderation and exposure design redistribute the public sphere; Van Dijck/Poell/de Waal (2018) provides a comprehensive overview of social infrastructuring as a tripartite market, government, platform Pasquale (2015) and Zuboff (2019) analyze empowerment as [black-boxing] and [surveillance capitalism]. ([Yale University Press https://yalebooks.yale.edu/book/9780300261431/custodians-of-the-internet/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
placement
With the above classics (Coase/Williamson/Powell/Ostrom), the frame of the triangle is established,
The Lessig/Yeung/Gillespie/Van Dijck lineage demonstrated "algo-distribution "**, which is neither price, command, nor norm, and its social range.

Furthermore, if we stand independently of simultaneous simultaneous reallocations due to state coercion, we can endogenously model policy-induced and algo-induced reallocations - this is the academic underpinning of the pentopole model.

lines.text: The Toxic Meme of the Right to Privacy
[GPT5.icon]
[** Adult Public].
The monument that stands in the center of the square is inscribed with a sentence from a past narrative.
>"Homo sapiens during this period were infected with the [harmful meme] of [privacy] rights."
No wonder," my grandmother shrugged. "That's when there was a spate of family murders because they couldn't see the CO levels in their neighbors' houses. It was polite to hide it."
Today is my [* adult reveal]. The lifeband on my wrist is unsealed and my breathing, sleep, mobility, purchasing, and neighborhood impact values are connected to my community.

Public disclosure is not punishment. It's [visibility of responsibility]. I alone have no right to cover up an area where my condition is directly related to the risk of others - that is our common sense.
Before the ritual, I am reminded of the recorded images I saw at school.

During the period of infection spread, contact networks were disrupted by walls of anonymity and cryptography, and exponential functions sprouted from the holes in tracking. Logistical delays were masked by trade secrets, and dialysis drugs disappeared city by city.

Once the open standards were implemented, the local mortality rate dropped 42% and the average arrival time for emergency services was 7 minutes shorter. This is because everyone can now see cause and effect and share [counterfactuals].
But what about [shame] or [weakness]?" I asked him once when I was very young.

My grandmother laughed and flicked her finger at the lifeband. Shame isn't protected by secrecy," she said. It is protected by context. We "only open our sphere of influence. lines.text: Organize iPhone tabs on your Mac
[GPT5.icon]
Yes, Safari on Mac can organize it (assuming iCloud tab sync); Windows alone practically can't.
Close iPhone tabs on Mac
1. turn on iCloud Safari sync on both (iPhone: Settings -> My Name -> iCloud -> Safari, Mac: System Settings -> Apple ID -> iCloud -> Safari) ([Apple Support https://support.apple.com/en-us/ 108409])

Open Safari on your Mac and go to the menu "Bookmarks" -> "Show Start Page". You will see a list of the tabs you have open on your iPhone in the iCloud tab at the bottom. Control-click on the tab → "Close Tab". ([Apple Support https://support.apple.com/en-us/108409])
Batch organization by tab group (Mac)

By right-clicking on a tab group in the sidebar -> "Delete", you can close all tabs in that group at once (and close the iPhone side during synchronization). ([iGeeksBlog https://www.igeeksblog.com/use-tab-groups-in-safari-on-iphone-ipad-mac/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
supplement

There is no official way to view/manipulate iCloud tabs on a Windows PC. Organize them from your iPhone OR Mac. ([Reddit https://www.reddit.com/r/apple/comments/aj3kic/icloud_tabs_on_windows/?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
If tab syncing is unstable, try turning off "Safari in iCloud" on the iPhone/Mac and then turning it back on to try syncing again. ([Apple Support https://support.apple.com/en-us/108409])

[East India Company] and [personal money].
[GPT5.icon]
EIC（English East India Company）
Official name: British East India Company
Founded: Royal Charter of Elizabeth I, 1600.
CORE: A chartered company granted a monopoly on trade in the East. In the early years, the company was a voyage-by-voyage investment (partnership); after 1657, it became a permanent joint stock.
Authority: substantial use of quasi-state powers such as diplomacy, tax collection, and use of force (especially in India).
Demise: In 1858, the Indian administration was transferred to the British government, and the company was dissolved in 1874.
VOC（Vereenigde Oostindische Compagnie）
Official name: Dutch East India Company
Founded: 1602.
CORE: Famous for being one of the world's early permanent joint stock companies. Shares traded on the open market (Amsterdam Exchange). Exclusive rights to trade in Asia.
Authority: quasi-state powers such as treaty-making, minting, garrisoning, etc.
Demise: Dissolved in 1799.
Both are historical models that "bundle large-scale risk with investor capital and scale it with corporate vessels".
However, it is a weak direct metaphor for the issue of whether "[employees] are willing to pay for it" (the money is mainly on the side of investors).
[** What is Permanent Joint Stock?]
In a nutshell, it is a system that permanently binds the capital of a company not "by voyage or project" but "the company itself" and allows the shares to be freely traded.
(= joint stock in which the capital is not settled at the end of the deal and lasts as long as the company continues to exist)
What's the point?
Permanence of capital: The capital contribution is not dissolved or returned at the end of the project.
Transferability of shares: investors can buy and sell their interests for cash (the company does not need to be dissolved). Secondary market established.
Limited liability (historically maintained): investor losses are limited in principle to the amount of the investment.
Dividends are based on "company-wide profit": dividends are paid from the company's overall profit/loss, not by voyage.
[Organizational continuity: Long-term investments and large-scale projects are possible because the corporation and capital continue even if people are replaced.
Different from what?
Voyage association (investment per project)
Investment in units of projects → Settlement and dissolution at the end of the project. Low liquidity of shares, not suitable for long-term capital investment or large-scale governance.
Why is it important?
Financial technology that made possible huge, long-term, and uncertain projects (overseas trade, infrastructure, colonies, and in later years, railroads and telegraphs).
Liquidity for investors and a stable supply of capital for the company.
At the same time, it also created [separation of ownership and management]/governance issues ([agency problems]).

→ In summary, the permanent joint stock is the core specification of the modern joint stock company. It is a mechanism that allows capital to be sustained in the "container of the company" and achieves liquidity and diversification in the stock market.

lines.text: Unified organizational culture lowers transaction costs in the organizational marketplace.
from  [Nodal point of thought 2025-09-30]
Unified organizational culture lowers transaction costs in the organizational marketplace.
[nishio.icon]
Unifying culture within an organization lowers [Transaction costs] in [Internal Market].
That makes it more efficient than trading on the market outside the organization.
This is why the organization exists.
Lower [decision-making costs] and [communication costs
[GPT5.icon]
Short fact check.

It is generally true that "an organization is established when it can coordinate at "lower transaction costs" than the market. Kors (1937) explained that markets, which use the price mechanism, have transaction costs such as contracting, searching, and bargaining, and that firms expand to the extent that the coordination costs of internal organizations are lower than these costs. Williamson extended the choice of "market, hierarchy (internal), and intermediate forms" according to the attributes of the transaction (asset specificity, uncertainty, and frequency). ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1468-0335.1937.tb00002.x?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Consistent with the main theory, "culture unification lowers transaction costs in the internal "market. Ouchi argued that "clan governance," or shared values and norms, can reduce valuation ambiguity and goal discrepancies, and save on supervision and contracting costs. ([JSTOR https://www.jstor.org/stable/2392231?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

There is theoretical support for "decision-making costs and communication costs will also go down." Arrow points out that organizations have channels for communication and decision-making that reduce the cost of cooperation without relying solely on price. Furthermore, Kogut & Zander's theory of the knowledge-based firm (Kogut & Zander), that "firms share and transfer knowledge better than markets," is compatible with the mechanism by which a common language, routines, and norms (culture) reduce communication costs. ([Google Books https://books.google.com/books/about/The_Limits_of_Organization.html?id=55eDQgAACAAJ&utm_source=chatgpt.com])

However, it is an oversimplification to go as far as "this is the entire reason for the organization's existence". The rationale of companies has developed in a multilinear way, including the integration of capabilities and knowledge (capability perspective), in addition to transaction costs. In some situations, markets and hybrid contracts are more efficient. ([IDEAS/RePEc https://ideas.repec.org/a/inm/ororsc/v3y1992i3p383-397.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Practical note: Culture is a double-edged sword: excessive homogeneity can lead to rigidity, false consensus (groupthink), and reduced adaptability, and in turn, increased decision-making and information acquisition costs - some empirical and field suggestions. ([Science Direct https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0304405X22001684?utm_source=chatgpt.com])
summary

The arguments you present are consistent with (1) Coase/Williamson's transaction cost theory, (2) Ouchi's "clan governance" = governance by culture, and (3) the knowledge-based view of the firm, and are generally correct in their direction. However, it is appropriate to strike a balance that includes factors such as transaction attributes and capabilities, and the possibility of selecting hybrid forms, rather than assuming that they are the "sole reason for existence. ([Wiley Online Library https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1468-0335.1937.tb00002.x?utm_source=chatgpt.com])

Just a quick point 👇.
What article?

Case study of Bowling Green, Kentucky (population approx. 75,000, projected to double in 25 years), where citizen feedback was collected by [Polis] and summarized and categorized by Jigsaw's AI tool [Sensemaker] for the "BG2050" long-term plan (published 4/15/2025). ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])
implementation method

Conducted a one-month online dialogue "What Could BG Be?" Approximately 8,000 people participated, voting for and against thousands of unique proposals over 1 million times. Input is open-ended design. ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])
Role of AI (Sensemaker)

Automatically clusters submissions into 12 topics and 72 subtopics to visualize support and polarization (mixed opinion). Generates reports in minutes, shortening analysis that would otherwise take days or weeks. ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])
Major Findings

A surprisingly wide agreement was found with the majority (2,370) having an agreement rate of over 80%. In addition to transportation and roads, nightlife/entertainment, art and festivals, green space, and community pride emerged as priorities. ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])

Differentiation of interest between K-12 and higher education (practical skills education vs. economic impact of college). ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])

Local context + human review is essential (e.g., understanding the background of riverfront development). ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])
Impact measurement (post-questionnaire)

Seventy percent of participants said that they felt more confident that their voices would be heard, and 83% said that they had a better understanding of different perspectives / better planning. Leaders rated the report as saving an average of 28 days of man-hours. ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])
Scale Effects

Enables incorporation of almost 80 times the number of citizens into a plan originally considered by 100 leaders. Suggests lateral expansion to other cities as a prototype for large-scale, continuous consensus building. ([Medium https://medium.com/jigsaw/how-one-of-the-fastest-growing-cities-in-kentucky-used-ai-to-plan-for-the-next-25-years-3b70c4fd 1412])
Suggestion (if you want to put it into practice).
1. design questions broadly and freely, and collect a large number of evaluations (pros and cons)
2. quickly summarize, cluster, and map agreement and conflict with AI
3) Interpret with local knowledge and take measures from high-consensus areas, and dig deeper in polarized areas.

4. measuring psychological and administrative effects through post-event questionnaires - quantitatively demonstrating "a sense of having one's voice heard" and usefulness in decision-making (also effective in providing a budgetary basis)

If necessary, we will create prompt design and dashboard indicators (consensus rate, mixed opinion level, topic granularity, geographic tags, etc.) for this BG case study in a ready-to-use template for Japanese local governments/organizations.
